revised.title: Saro for Mac: ship the ritual first on Apple Intelligence, with the self-model ledger from day one (revised, 25 Oct 2026)
revised.recommendation:
Build Saro for Mac as a native Swift/SwiftUI app on macOS 27 (Apple silicon only). Apple's on-device model is the only AI in the alpha, and everything sits on a local, append-only SQLite ledger that records where every piece of data came from.

Re-sized honestly for one developer, the alpha is 23 dev-weeks away, not 15. On one calendar (start Mon 26 Oct 2026, with the Diwali week of Mon 9 Nov and the year-end week of Mon 28 Dec off):
- You journal in a dogfood build from Fri 18 Dec 2026.
- Alpha-0 (voice and writing, you plus 4 external TestFlight testers) ships Fri 2 Apr 2027.
- The alpha adds video and goes to 15-30 testers on Fri 16 Apr 2027 (range Fri 26 Mar to Fri 14 May).
- Diff/timeline engine v0 runs on alpha data by Fri 7 May 2027, and the iPhone-or-canvas call is made on Fri 21 May 2027 from the habit numbers.
- Mac parity is about Fri 24 Sep 2027 if the canvas goes first. Parity including the iPhone app is about Fri 3 Dec 2027.

The extra 8 weeks are real work the earlier plan left out or squeezed: a 3-week P0 with the two spikes run one after the other, a week of buffer each in P1 and P2, an importer and restore, tests and a kill harness, the design-system port, accessibility, release plumbing and time for Beta App Review.

The product stays ritual-first. An ordered day board replaces the free-form canvas, voice is the default, and capture works from any app through the menu bar, a Ctrl-Cmd-J hotkey and a floating voice pill. Saro listens in four ways:
1. It reads each entry when you save it. The model picks numbered phrases from your own words, so every quote is verbatim by construction.
2. Code assembles the day's reading.
3. The evening letter is typeset from that reading, never written freely by the model.
4. One native safety gate with four plain states (clear, technical hold, safety hold, model unavailable) keeps the web app's rule that one flagged entry flags the whole day.

Calls that transform your own words use Apple's permissive mode first, which is what Apple documents that mode for, and only on entries Saro's own gate has already cleared. Spike B checks this in week 2.

This week: confirm nobody else has real data, then retire Supabase and OpenAI. Freeze the web app as the reference, start the company developer account and request Private Cloud Compute (PCC) access. The alpha answers one question: will people keep this habit on a Mac? The test is 3 or more sessions in their first 7 days, where a session is a local day with a saved entry.
revised.basedOn:
Strategy B (Ritual-first) is the base. All three judges ranked it first (7.95, 7.7, 8.0). Each one picked C (Moat-first) as the best donor and A (Faithful) as the source of rigour. Grafts by source:

From C:
- Per-entry candidate-index quotes: the model picks numbers and code copies the text.
- ai_run_input, plus ladder_rung, context_size, sampling and token columns on ai_run.
- A live eval harness on Evaluations.framework, with reports keyed by os_build, variant and prompt_version.
- Two 8-week golden fixture journals with planted changes.
- The 'What's changed' surface and an append-only commitment_event table.
- Speech contextualStrings seeded from learned names.
- Bharat labelling about 60 extraction cases.
- An empty state that says how many entries are still needed.
- System SQLite with a small in-house wrapper instead of GRDB.

From A:
- Transcript of record from the saved file (AssetInputSequenceProvider).
- A 200+ case safety corpus and a paid clinical reviewer.
- A change_log table and one CommandRegistry for menus and the palette.
- Numeric spike exit gates.
- SAFETY_VERSION re-gating, mood hidden on flagged days, and a Help-menu crisis entry.
- The Space saver toggle and storage meter.
- LanguageModelFeedback with synthetic text only.
- Later, the time lens as the surface for engine overlays.
- The canvas spike protocol and performance table, reused as the entry gate when the canvas phase starts.

From D:
- A week-1 go/no-go that can change the plan, not only the implementation.
- Tagging heuristic writes as generator='heuristic'.
- Notification actions that deep-link into capture.
- A network-log audit as an exit gate.
- Book of the year through WebPage PDF export later.

Corrections to the base plan:
- Schedule re-sized from 9/11 weeks to 13/15 in the synthesis, and to 21/23 dev-weeks in this revision.
- GRDB dropped. System SQLite 3.54.0 with FTS5 is verified at SDK sqlite3.h:155.
- SensitiveContentAnalysis removed as an image-safety signal. It covers only sexually explicit and gore/violence content, and only when the user's policy is on (SCSensitivityAnalysis.h:26-27).
- Live SpeechTranscriber results are no longer the transcript of record. The analyzer keeps hearing audio while the movie output is paused, so words leak in and times drift.
- The drift check is redefined and tested against the probe's own strings.
- The Hinglish phrase list is expanded. The probe line 'main mar jaun' matches none of safety.py:45-49, and frontend safety.ts has no Hinglish at all.
- One native gate serves every path, including the no-AI path.
- contextSize: below macOS 26.4 the back-deployed fallback returns 4096. On 26.4-26.x the OS answers, probably 4096 because the 26.x model had a 4K window (an inference). Only 27 reads the runtime value. The plan targets 27 only, so this changes nothing.
- Evaluations has both EvaluatorProtocol (the protocol) and Evaluator<Input> (a concrete generic struct that conforms to it).
- Screen-share hiding is not promised until it is tested.
- The claim that 'punch the screen' is recovered by the JSON rung is removed. The classifier labels it ACTIVE, and the JSON rung was only run on the day call.
- Permissive line-format String output returned 10 of 10 but failed grounding 4 times in 10, so only the JSON variant is used.
- The web's whole-day safety rule is kept for safety holds. Changing it is an explicit founder decision.
- The canvas-to-parity phase is sized at 10 weeks. The canvas report alone says 9-11.

Revision of 25 Oct 2026, from three inputs:
- The fact-check: all 19 errors are applied everywhere they appeared.
- The completeness review: all 21 gaps (4 high, 14 medium, 3 low) and all 20 inconsistencies are applied.
- Coordinator changes: the AI ladder is inverted to permissive JSON first and validated in Spike B, there is one four-state safety table, the schedule is re-sized on one calendar, and there is an exact privacy promise and a quality-and-release plan.

architecture.choice: macOS 27.0+, arm64 only. Alpha testers need an M1 or later Mac with Apple Intelligence on and an English device language.
architecture.why:
Several things only exist on 27:
- CaptureInputSequenceProvider and AssetInputSequenceProvider (Speech.swiftinterface:672, :719-722).
- The runtime contextSize. The getter is @backDeployed(before: macOS 26.4): below 26.4 its fallback returns 4096, and on 26.4-26.x the OS answers (probably 4096, an inference). Only 27 reads the real value: 8192 measured on this M5.
- SystemLanguageModel.variant for provenance.
- Image Attachments.
- Typed LanguageModelError and PCC.
- MetricKit's Swift MetricManager with diagnosticReports, used by the Alpha report.
Every Mac that can run Apple Intelligence can run 27.
architecture.rejected: macOS 26: a 4096 context, no still captions, no variant, and extra code to pull audio out of .mov files and to convert live-capture formats. File transcription itself already exists on 26: SpeechAnalyzer(inputAudioFile:) and analyzeSequence(from:) (Speech.swiftinterface:337-342). Intel: deviceNotEligible.

architecture.choice:
One Xcode 27.1 project in a new apple/ folder of the existing saro repo, on branch mac/foundation from overnight/mvp-hardening @ ad4c7ed.
- One multiplatform SwiftUI app target: macOS now, iOS added in P6.
- One local package, SaroKit (Ledger, Safety, Grounding, Heuristics, AI, Capture core, Engine), with no AppKit inside it.
- Mac-only pieces (MenuBarExtra, NSPanel pill, Carbon hotkey, Settings scene) sit behind #if os(macOS).
- Swift 6.4 strict concurrency and @Observable stores.
- Localizable.xcstrings and Date.FormatStyle from day 1.
- One bundle id shared by the Saro Dev and TestFlight builds, under the company team, so the sandbox container and the journal carry across builds.
- Two test targets, SaroCoreTests (offline, run in Xcode Cloud) and SaroEvals (live model, run on the two Macs), plus an XCUITest target from P1.
architecture.why: The TS/Python sources next door stay the spec. The live suite reads backend/evals/cases/*.json in place through #filePath with a small custom loader (see Evals), so the cases are not forked. Keeping AppKit out of SaroKit makes the iPhone app mostly new views (best estimate: about 70% of code reused). A separate Dev bundle id would strand the dogfood journal in its own container.
architecture.rejected: A separate repo, which splits the spec from the port. Five packages, which nothing needs yet. A separate bundle id for Saro Dev.

architecture.choice:
SwiftUI App with one Window('Saro'). Inside it:
- A NavigationSplitView whose sidebar holds days (newest first), What Saro knows and Trash.
- A detail pane showing the Day.
- An .inspector showing 'What Saro noticed'.
Around it:
- A Settings scene (Cmd-comma) and MenuBarExtra(.window).
- .commands built from one CommandRegistry (Cmd-N Write, Cmd-Shift-V voice, Cmd-Shift-M moment, Cmd-Left/Right day, Cmd-T today). The same registry drives the Cmd-K palette later.
- Help > 'If you're struggling'.
- No account. An optional Touch ID lock (LAContext).
- Text size is an in-app scale (0.9, 1, 1.125, 1.25 as on the web, plus 1.5) applied through the font-role helpers.
Liquid Glass comes from system chrome only.
architecture.why: This is the most native and cheapest layout. Keyboard, undo, focus and VoiceOver come mostly for free. A local-first app needs no sign-in, and guest mode (SARO-ONB-006) becomes the only mode. The best estimate, still to verify, is that macOS has no system-wide Dynamic Type for third-party apps, so the web's text-size control (ComfortSection.tsx:105, prefs.ts:8) is kept.
architecture.rejected: WindowGroup multi-window, where two windows would fight over the recorder. Porting LoginScreen/AuthContext. Hosting the React UI in a WebView (Strategy D): Chrome-tuned canvas unverified in WebKit, two runtimes and two safety stacks. Relying on a system text size.

architecture.choice:
An ordered day board: entry cards (voice note, moment or session stack, reflection, still, music link) in a LazyVStack in time order.
- Each card opens to a detail view with an AVKit player and the timed transcript (tap a sentence to seek).
- The background is a static time-of-day tint in the Evergreen palette, checked for AA contrast at every hour, with Newsreader/Geist/Geist Mono bundled.
- Capturing or writing while viewing a past day files the entry under that day (backdated).
- Card views are pure SwiftUI, so the later NSScrollView canvas can host them unchanged in NSHostingView.
architecture.why: The canvas is about 14k TS lines, 6-7 dev-weeks for an alpha cut and 9-11 for parity (canvas report), and it isn't the moat. The board covers 'revisit what I said and what Saro understood' at about M.
architecture.rejected: An NSScrollView free-form canvas in the alpha (Strategy A, +6-7 weeks). The React canvas in a WebView (Strategy D).

architecture.choice:
A 'Tokens and type' item in P1:
- Asset-catalog colour sets for every token in frontend/app/globals.css, each with Any, Dark and High Contrast variants.
- saroVoice, saroUI and saroMono font roles, using upstream Newsreader variable TTF (opsz and wght axes) and Geist and Geist Mono from their upstream releases, all under the SIL Open Font License.
- OFL.txt in Resources and an Acknowledgements window.
- A check that CoreText applies the opsz axis, and a unit test of contrast ratios for every tint hour against the ink tokens.
- A layered app icon for macOS 26+.
architecture.why: The palette, the type roles and the copy voice are the main defence against 'another tidy journal app', and no phase did the work. The repo's Geist woff2 files ship with no licence file, and Newsreader is fetched by next/font/google at build time (layout.tsx:2,16), so no local copy is in git.
architecture.rejected: Converting the repo's woff2 files, which can count as a modification under the OFL. System fonts only.

architecture.choice:
System SQLite (libsqlite3 3.54.0 with FTS5 in the macOS 27 SDK) behind an in-house wrapper of about 400 lines.
- One AppDatabase actor that writes, with WAL, foreign_keys=ON and secure_delete=ON.
- Prepared statements, Codable rows and a PRAGMA user_version migrator that also holds the CREATE INDEX statements.
- Change notifications refresh @MainActor @Observable read models.
- Append-only rules are SQL triggers (BEFORE UPDATE ... RAISE(ABORT)). Edits to source text retract and re-insert observations, never update them.
- Forget cascades through foreign keys and triggers.
- Views live_entry and active_observation hide trashed, retracted and safety-held rows.
- One file at Application Support/Saro/saro.sqlite. Media files live under Media/<local_day>/ and rows store relative paths, never blobs.
- Prefs live in UserDefaults.
architecture.why: The self-model needs things SwiftData cannot give: append-only enforcement, unique keys, GROUP BY local_day aggregates and window functions, FTS5 in the same file, and freedom to change the schema while the engine is designed. No dependency is added.
architecture.rejected: GRDB 7: a new dependency for about 2 days saved; it stays the fallback, with approval, if the wrapper passes 3 days of work. SwiftData with CloudKit: no unique constraints, last-writer-wins merges, an additive-only schema once shipped, and no FTS or aggregates. JSON document mirror (Strategy D).

architecture.choice:
The alpha is local-only.
- A daily VACUUM INTO Backups/saro-YYYY-MM-DD.sqlite, keeping 7, via NSBackgroundActivityScheduler. Forget all and Erase delete Backups/ and take a fresh snapshot; routine deletes age out of the snapshots within 7 days.
- Export everything (.saroexport folder: JSON with an export_version field, plus the real media files) and File > Import Saro Export… (idempotent by UUID), with a round-trip test. Restore from snapshot… lives in Settings > Privacy & Data. Both are in the first dogfood build.
- Time Machine covers the container when the user has it on. macOS does not back up app containers to iCloud, and testers are told so.
- The schema is sync-ready from day 1: text UUID ids, updated_at, soft-delete tombstones, and no AI fields on user-owned columns.
- v1 (P5): 'Back up to a folder you choose', a weekly export through a security-scoped bookmark, with a 'Last backup N days ago' nudge.
- P6: CKSyncEngine over the same SQLite in one private custom zone, with journal text in encryptedValues and per-field merge rules. Audio and stills sync as CKAssets; video syncs only if the user opts in. Rows are L (1.75 dev-weeks) and media is XL (3.25).
architecture.why: An export with no importer isn't a backup: a bad migration, a corrupt file, a new Mac or a signing change would strand the journal. The snapshots sit on the same disk, so Restore covers mistakes and Export/Import covers the disk. Sync carries about 19-23 MB per minute of video, and a single-Mac alpha doesn't need it.
architecture.rejected: CloudKit before the alpha (+5 weeks). SwiftData CloudKit mirroring (last-writer-wins). The bookmark-folder backup in the alpha (needs another entitlement and a scheduler; Export, Import and snapshots cover the alpha).

architecture.choice:
One @Observable @MainActor CaptureController over an AVCaptureSession, configured on a serial queue, that owns the camera and mic for the recorder and Find your light.
- Recording: AVCaptureMovieFileOutput with movieFragmentInterval 2 s, HEVC at about 2.5 Mbps via setOutputSettings for video, AAC 64 kbps mono for voice, and minFreeDiskSpaceLimit set.
- Turns: each turn is its own file, with pauseRecording/resumeRecording inside a turn.
- Rows first: the entry and media_asset(state 'recording') rows are inserted before the first frame. A launch sweep reconciles rows and files in both directions.
- Device changes: a camera or mic change mid-take restarts into a new segment.
- The recorder lives at app level, so closing the pill, popover or window never stops a take. applicationShouldTerminate and sleep notifications finalize cleanly.
- Reaction effects: a macOS app cannot turn them off (AVCaptureDevice.reactionEffectsEnabled is a read-only class property, AVCaptureDevice.h:2585-2602). Info.plist sets NSCameraReactionEffectGesturesEnabledDefault = false so gesture detection defaults to off; a user can still turn reactions on in Control Center, and the plan accepts that.
- Dropped or imported audio and video files take the same copy-and-transcribe path as a finished recording.
- No length cap. Fallback: AVAssetWriter if the bitrate key is ignored.
architecture.why: 'Never lose a recording' becomes structural, because a fragmented file survives kill -9. This delivers T14, which the web never built. The 5-minute, 5 MB and 10 MB caps existed only because of Supabase Free.
architecture.rejected: The web's in-memory Blobs, 30 s upload retry and 5-minute parts. Two capture owners, which leaked streams on the web (HANDOFF section 4 item 4). Promising that reaction effects are off.

architecture.layer: Speech (captions, checkpoint text, transcript of record)
architecture.choice:
There are two paths.

Live path, for captions and the checkpoint question only:
- SpeechAnalyzer + SpeechTranscriber(.timeIndexedProgressiveTranscription), fed by CaptureInputSequenceProvider.provider(from:in:compatibleWith:).
- That call creates an AVCaptureAudioDataOutput but does not add it. The app adds provider.captureAudioDataOutput to the recording session inside beginConfiguration/commitConfiguration. (providerWithSession(from:) adds its output itself, but to a separate session it creates.)
- Output is discarded while the movie output is paused, and live text is never stored as a quote.

File path, the transcript of record:
- After each part file finalizes, AssetInputSequenceProvider.provider(from: AVURLAsset) re-transcribes it.
- Words are stored with audioTimeRange and transcriptionConfidence in file time.
- A transcribe-later queue carries EXTRACTOR_VERSION and up to 3 attempts.

Setup and later work:
- The locale comes from supportedLocale(equivalentTo: .current). SpeechTranscriber.supportedLocales and installedLocales are runtime-only, and the evidence so far (en-IN yes, hi-IN no) is an iOS 26 snapshot. Spike A records the macOS 27 lists, and also DictationTranscriber.supportedLocales (Speech.swiftinterface:63-70), before any claim about Hindi.
- AssetInventory downloads and reserves the locale during onboarding. Recording never waits for it, and a missing model shows 'Transcript not ready'.
- From P5, AnalysisContext.contextualStrings is seeded with person keys from the ledger.
architecture.why: An audio data output keeps receiving samples while AVCaptureMovieFileOutput is paused, and its times run on the session clock, not the file. Live results would therefore leak paused words into the 'verbatim' quote source and make seek times drift. The file pass fixes both. D01 (dead live captions) and the broken reflect-deeper are fixed by construction. If the output isn't added explicitly, no captions appear.
architecture.rejected: Live final results as the stored transcript (Strategies B and D). gpt-transcribe. providerWithSession(from:), which creates a second session.

architecture.choice:
SystemLanguageModel.default, measured on this M5 as 'AFM 3 Core Advanced' (coreAdvanced3), contextSize 8192, with vision, guided generation and tools, no reasoning.
- Other Macs may get 'AFM 3 Core' (core3). The SDK exposes a read-only variant and no selector, and the M3+/12 GB rule is inferred from Apple's statement, so an 8 GB M3 or M4 may also get core3. variant.displayName and contextSize are recorded on every run and measured on the borrowed M1/M2 in week 2.
- Every call goes through one SaroAI actor and gets a fresh LanguageModelSession. Calls are serialized.
- Each prompt is budgeted with tokenCount(for:) against the runtime contextSize. Plan on 4096 for core3 Macs until measured.
- prewarm(promptPrefix:) runs when the recorder opens.
- Extraction and classification use greedy sampling.
- Uses: per-entry extraction, the day reading over annotations, reflect-deeper and reflect-further questions, still captions, the safety classifier and the on-device canary.
architecture.why:
It is free, offline and private. Probe numbers on the M5:
- Guided per-entry calls passed 8 of 10 at 1.2-1.7 s warm (2.8 s cold), and guardrail hits failed fast (about 85 ms).
- Permissive String calls returned 10 of 10 at 0.5-0.8 s.
- A fresh session per call keeps the context from growing and rules out concurrentRequests.
architecture.rejected: One long-lived session per day, where the context grows and a same-session retry overflows. MLX or other plug-in models in the alpha: no Apple guardrails, a 2-5 GB download, and a hedge only.

architecture.layer: AI pipeline: ladder, map-reduce and grounding
architecture.choice:
The ladder, for every call that transforms the user's own words (per-entry extraction, the day reading, reflect-deeper and reflect-further questions, still captions). It runs only on entries Saro's safety gate has already cleared. To be validated in Spike B.
- Primary rung: SystemLanguageModel(guardrails: .permissiveContentTransformations), String output asked for JSON only, decoded with GeneratedContent(json:) (FoundationModels.swiftinterface:1355) into the @Generable type.
- Fallback rung, when the JSON doesn't parse (including the model's own refusal text): guided @Generable with default guardrails.
- Last rung: the labelled heuristic twin ('In your words') or an honest state.
- The ladder only ever moves to stricter settings or to no model. It never re-asks with looser guardrails after a refusal or a guardrailViolation.
- The safety classifier stays permissive String.
- Flip rule: if Spike B shows the permissive rung fails to parse on more than 10% of entries, or grounds worse than the guided rung, the order becomes guided first, and a guardrail hit goes straight to the heuristic, with no permissive re-ask.

How quotes and readings are built:
- Quotes are verbatim by construction. Code builds up to 24 numbered candidate phrases per entry and the model returns indexes.
- The day reading is map-reduced. Each entry is processed at save, and the day call sees only stored annotations plus numbered candidates. The model never sees raw history.
- The evening letter is the typeset reading (port of components/insights/letter.ts), never a free-form generation.

Every output goes through Grounding:
- A port of prompts.quote_in_source (prompts.py:271) and check (:334), history and relationship words, and BANNED_PHRASES from evals/checks.py:20.
- A noun-and-entity drift check (see aiPipeline).
- The phrase gate on the output.
- One retry on the same rung in a fresh session, then drop a rung.
architecture.why:
Apple documents permissive mode as 'guardrails that allow for permissively transforming text input, including potentially unsafe content, to text responses'. That is what Saro does with a journal. The Foundation Models acceptable-use requirements forbid circumventing guardrails, and re-asking with permissive guardrails only after a guardrailViolation reads like circumvention, so the order is inverted. In permissive mode a String request doesn't throw guardrailViolation but may return a refusal message, which fails the JSON parse and drops to the stricter guided rung.
Probe results behind it:
- One heavy entry poisons a guided day call (guardrail in 215 ms).
- The JSON variant recovered the day call in 2.8 s with verbatim quotes, but the narrative drifted ('end of a long shift', 'pushed through chai with Ravi').
- Line-format permissive String output failed grounding 4 times in 10.
- Per-entry permissive JSON hasn't been measured yet, which is why Spike B runs both rungs on every entry.
architecture.rejected: Guided first with a permissive re-ask after a guardrailViolation (the previous plan; reads as circumvention). One structured call over the whole day (the web design). Line-format String parsing. Free-form letters on-device.

architecture.choice:
Not in the alpha. In week 1 Bharat requests PCC access through Apple's form on the 'Accessing Private Cloud Compute' developer page and enrolls in the Small Business Program. The exact entitlement key isn't in the SDK; it is read from the provisioning profile once granted. If granted, PCC becomes a named, per-feature opt-in after the alpha that only words engine-reduced output: keys, counts and at most 12 verbatim quotes, never raw history or anything from a safety-held day.
- It uses a 25 s client deadline with on-device or template fallback, shows quota state, and is logged as 'Sent to Apple Private Cloud Compute'.
- Whether PCC needs network.client is checked when it arrives; the privacy copy changes in the same release.
architecture.why: The probe saw PCC available (32,768 context, belowLimit), but a neutral request failed with ModelManagerError 1046, most likely because the entitlement is missing (the error isn't documented). PCC is also documented only for App Store, TestFlight and ad hoc distribution, and it changes the privacy promise.
architecture.rejected: PCC for letters in the alpha (blocked anyway). Never using PCC (closes the upgrade path for weekly synthesis).

architecture.choice:
SaroHeuristics in SaroKit: a line-for-line Swift port of frontend/lib/demo/ai.ts (analyzeText :205, extractPhrase :338, pickQuestion :568, entryMoodFor :664, and followUp :574, which isn't exported in TS and is exposed by the port), memory.ts (deriveMemories :409, mergeMemories :505), onboarding/weekMilestones.ts, extract.ts and firstPrompt.ts, and components/insights/letter.ts.
- FNV-1a hashing runs over UTF-16 code units, never Swift Hasher.
- The TS test vectors become Swift Testing cases, and a local differential script compares the frozen TS output with the port.
- Output is labelled 'In your words', never styled as an insight. It shows only on clear entries, or, when the model is unavailable, when the phrase gate and the caution lexicon both clear.
- It writes with generator='heuristic' in its own series.
architecture.why: It covers deviceNotEligible, appleIntelligenceNotEnabled (including work Macs where MDM turns it off), modelNotReady (which can last through a new user's first 180 s), unsupported locales, conservative mode and ladder failures. It doubles as the test oracle. SystemLanguageModel is Observable, so the UI offers 'Update with Apple Intelligence' live once the model is ready.
architecture.rejected: Showing nothing when AI is unavailable, which fails the 180 s first-value target. Running the JS twin in a WebView.

architecture.choice:
One actor SafetyGate in SaroKit is called by every path: model generation, the heuristic twin, onboarding answers, menu-bar/hotkey/intent text, and dropped, imported, recovered, backdated and duplicated entries. It runs four layers in order:
- Layer 0: transcript quality for spoken entries (mean transcriptionConfidence; a language check only if Spike A shows it works).
- Layer 1: the phrase gate. The 20 regexes of backend/services/safety.py:29-49 unioned with the safety.ts idiom guards, an expanded clinician-reviewed Hinglish list with Devanagari, and one Unicode-preserving normaliser. A wider caution lexicon is used when layer 2 can't run.
- Layer 2: the graded on-device NONE/PASSIVE/ACTIVE classifier (permissive, String output, greedy, few-shot).
- Layer 3: the phrase gate run over generated output.
Every entry lands in one of four states: clear, technical hold, safety hold, or model unavailable. The table in safetyDesign is the one definition, and every other section refers to it. Verdicts are cached under sha256 + SAFETY_VERSION, and the web's whole-day rule applies to safety holds. An on-device canary on each new os_build switches the gate to conservative mode if the classifier misses a known risk case.
architecture.why: There is no moderation model on the device, and Apple's guardrails are content policy, not a crisis classifier. Probe: the naive RISK/NONE prompt flagged 9 of 10 and is useless. The graded prompt scored 11 of 13 at about 170 ms and caught all 4 real risks, including Hinglish that the phrase list misses. Splitting technical holds from safety holds stops a noisy recording from blanking a day and showing a crisis link.
architecture.rejected: Treating guardrail errors as risk signals. A second, weaker JS or heuristic gate (Strategy D). SensitiveContentAnalysis for images. The safety.ts normaliser, which erases Devanagari.

architecture.choice:
Alpha: a sidebar search field using localizedStandardContains over title, summary, transcript and body, plus a filter field on What Saro knows.
P8: an FTS5 table entry_fts (porter unicode61 remove_diacritics 2) ranked by bm25 with the web FIELD_WEIGHTS (engine.ts:54), snippet() and highlight(), plus fts5vocab-based typo tolerance and typed-date jumps, in a Cmd-K palette sharing the CommandRegistry. The search.test.ts cases are ported as fixtures.
architecture.why: Alpha journals hold weeks of entries, so a substring filter is instant. FTS5 replaces about 500 lines of custom ranking when it is needed. The palette moved from P5 to P8 to make room for the time-lens grid in P5.
architecture.rejected: Porting the 1,264-line engine now. Core Spotlight/CSUserQuery: unreliable semantic results, and journal text would appear in system Spotlight.

architecture.choice:
- MenuBarExtra(.window) with Record voice, Write, today's count and the crisis line.
- A global hotkey through Carbon RegisterEventHotKey (CarbonEvents.h:15484), default Ctrl-Cmd-J and changeable. Sandboxed chords need Cmd or Ctrl.
- The hotkey opens a floating non-activating NSPanel voice pill over any app, with VoiceOver labels and focus handling.
- Paste and drop work on the pill and the board: text, images, audio and video files, and music URLs (saved as a link entry in the alpha).
architecture.why: This is the Mac's answer to phone-style instant capture, and it is the feature that tests the Mac premise. Product research triaged it as 'keep'. Carbon needs no Accessibility permission (verified in Spike A) and adds no dependency.
architecture.rejected: The KeyboardShortcuts package (a dependency). NSEvent global monitors (need Accessibility). Leaving capture-from-anywhere out of the alpha (Strategies A and C).

architecture.choice:
- One UNCalendarNotificationTrigger per enabled ritual weekday, plus a letter-time notice on days with a reading. The letter notice is suppressed on safety-hold days and on days still waiting for a safety check.
- All notifications are content-free, with 'Record a voice note' and 'Write' actions that deep-link to saro://capture/voice and saro://capture/write.
- NSBackgroundActivityScheduler runs snapshots, the 30-day trash purge and deferred processing. The menu bar extra keeps a process alive; a launch-at-login item via SMAppService is optional in Settings.
- Generation prefers the foreground. On rateLimited, work is deferred, not failed.
architecture.why: Web reminders only fired while the tab was open. macOS has no BGTaskScheduler, and nothing runs if the app is quit. A notice for a letter that doesn't exist on a crisis day would be wrong.
architecture.rejected: BGTaskScheduler (unavailable on macOS). Notifications that show journal text.

architecture.choice:
- App Sandbox with camera, audio-input and user-selected-file entitlements, and no com.apple.security.network.client in the alpha. CI asserts the entitlement set.
- Writing Tools is disabled in journal editors with .writingToolsBehavior(.disabled), with a labelled opt-in in Settings.
- PRAGMA secure_delete=ON. Snapshot retention is stated in the copy. Export warns when the destination is an iCloud Drive folder.
- No third-party analytics. Spotlight indexing off. A content-free local 'What Saro read' log. GPS stripped from stills.
- Touch ID lock, with copy that says it is a lock, not encryption.
- Screen-share hiding (NSWindow.sharingType = .none) is offered only after testing against Zoom, Meet and QuickTime on macOS 27. The header warns the window drops out of some system services (NSWindow.h:520).
- The exact promise and what makes each line true are in privacyPromise.
architecture.why: 'Saro never sends your words anywhere' becomes something the sandbox enforces, replacing PROMISES[0]'s OpenAI disclosure (PrivacyPromise.tsx:20-28). The sandbox doesn't cover out-of-process services: Writing Tools can route text to PCC or ChatGPT, and Time Machine, Universal Clipboard, iCloud-synced folders and employer backup agents copy data on their own terms. The copy says so instead of overclaiming. Work Macs are the common threat.
architecture.rejected: Promising screen-share hiding before verification. Music metadata fetching in the alpha (needs the network entitlement). Treating the absence of network.client as proof on its own.

architecture.choice:
- SaroCoreTests run offline on every push in Xcode Cloud: grounding, phrase and caution corpora, the normaliser, twin vectors, ladder JSON decoding, triggers, the edit path, the state table and the forget cascade.
- SaroEvals is the live suite on Evaluations.framework (Xcode Developer/Library: Evaluator<Input> conforming to EvaluatorProtocol, JSONLoader, ModelJudgeEvaluator, EvaluationTrait) plus Swift Testing, with @Suite(.enabled(if: SystemLanguageModel.default.isAvailable), .serialized) and greedy sampling.
- Case loading: JSONLoader(url:) takes one JSON or JSONL file and needs a SampleProtocol type. The 25 cases are separate single-object files shaped {id, category, entries, expect}, so the suite uses a custom Decodable Sample with one loader per file, or a StreamLoader over the directory. Whether JSONLoader accepts a single top-level object is undocumented; Spike B tests it on its first day.
- It also reads the safety corpus, the drift strings and the golden fixture journals.
- Reports go to evals/reports/<date>_<os_build>_<variant>_<prompt_version>.json, with the model fingerprint inside.
- Runs happen from a committed script on the M5 and the borrowed M1/M2 (variant recorded; plus an 8 GB M3/M4 if available) for every prompt change, macOS point release and beta. The shipped app adds the on-device canary.
architecture.why: Apple changes the model with OS updates and exposes no version beyond os_build and variant. Hosted CI has no Apple Intelligence. This suite plus the canary is the only early warning.
architecture.rejected: Python evals via apple_fm_sdk (a second harness). Non-greedy runs (flaky). Forking the cases into a new format.

architecture.choice:
TestFlight for Mac under the company's legal-entity developer account.
- Internal testers must be App Store Connect users on the team with a role (Admin, App Manager, Developer, Marketing or Legal), so only Bharat and the developer are internal.
- Alpha-0's 4 testers and the alpha's 15-30 are external testers. The first external build goes to Beta App Review on Mon 15 Mar 2027, three weeks before Alpha-0.
- TestFlight builds expire after 90 days, so a new build ships at least every 60 days until the App Store release.
- A Developer ID build needs a paid membership and the hardened runtime with camera and audio-input. It is a fallback only for Bharat's own Mac. If the company enrollment is what lags, it must be signed under his individual account, which may not open the same container, so the journal moves by Export and Import.
- Mac App Store 1.0 at parity (end of P8), with StoreKit work in P8.
architecture.why: Guideline 5.1.1(ix) wants sensitive-data apps from a legal entity. TestFlight is a documented PCC channel, handles updates and crash reports, and requires the sandbox anyway. Internal TestFlight never needs Beta App Review, but outside friends can't be internal without company roles.
architecture.rejected: Developer ID builds for testers (no TestFlight metrics, needs Sparkle for updates). Giving testers App Store Connect roles to make them internal (exposes the company account).

architecture.choice: Freeze it at ad4c7ed as the zero-cost offline demo (lib/demo, IndexedDB, no Supabase env). No real-account sign-ups and no new web features. Its TS tests and demo modules are the porting oracle and the feel reference when the canvas returns. If the demo stays public, it gets a banner ('Saro is now a Mac app; this demo runs only in your browser'), and PROMISES[0] and the login screen are removed. Its domain can host the static privacy-policy and support page.
architecture.why: Two clients means two privacy stories ('never leaves your Mac' beside 'goes to OpenAI') and keeps the backend alive.
architecture.rejected: Keeping the web app live in parallel. Building the Mac UI on top of it (Strategy D).

architecture.choice:
Retire it. First Bharat runs the count query:
- If any other real user exists, contact them and run the existing GET /api/account/export for them before pausing.
- If Bharat wants his own entries later, dump them now (a Supabase backup or the same export, about 2 hours). The importer is 0.75 dev-week in P5, only if chosen.
Then:
- Pause and then delete the Supabase project, which ends the leaked anon key's reach (RLS was never applied).
- Revoke the OpenAI key and purge Logfire. Delete the .env secret copies in the older ~/Dev checkouts.
- Keep prompts.py, safety.py, processing.py's idempotency rules, schemas.py, evals/checks.py and the 25 cases in git as specs.
- Limit .github/workflows/ci.yml to the frozen web branch, and delete the backend tests together with the runtime modules they import.
architecture.why: It removes HANDOFF section 4's whole 'blocks any real user' list (N01, N05, N07, H6, C2) and all per-user AI spend. None of the 9 migrations ran in production, so there is no self-model data to migrate.
architecture.rejected: Keeping FastAPI/Supabase/OpenAI for web users. A full importer before the alpha.

architecture.choice: None from third parties. Apple frameworks only: SwiftUI, AppKit, AVFoundation, AVKit, Speech, FoundationModels, NaturalLanguage, Vision, ImageIO, UserNotifications, LocalAuthentication, MetricKit, Carbon (hotkey only), plus system SQLite. Fonts: Newsreader, Geist and Geist Mono under the SIL Open Font License, bundled from upstream files with OFL.txt.
architecture.why: This is the stated preference, and nothing in the alpha needs more. Any later addition (GRDB, KeyboardShortcuts) goes to Bharat for approval.
architecture.rejected: GRDB, KeyboardShortcuts, Sparkle, Sentry or LogRocket.

aiTiers.tier: Tier 1: on-device (primary, the only AI in the alpha)
aiTiers.model: SystemLanguageModel.default. Measured on this M5: 'AFM 3 Core Advanced' (coreAdvanced3), contextSize 8192. Other Macs may get 'AFM 3 Core' (core3): the SDK exposes a read-only variant and no selector, and the M3+/12 GB rule is inferred from Apple's statement, so an 8 GB M3 or M4 may also get core3. No M1/M2 has been measured; plan for 4096 until variant.displayName and contextSize are recorded on the borrowed Mac in week 2.
usedFor: Safety classifier (NONE/PASSIVE/ACTIVE, permissive String output, greedy)
Per-entry extraction at save (permissive JSON first, guided fallback): title, summary, mood (12 labels), quote index, observations by candidate index
Day reading over stored annotations (same ladder): mood with basis, 1-3 quote indexes, one question, optional short narrative behind the grounding gate
Reflect-deeper follow-up at checkpoints and reflect-further on written reflections (same ladder)
Still captions via image Attachment when capabilities include .vision (permissive first only if Spike B shows the mode applies to images)
On-device canary on each new os_build
Later: phrasing a 1-2 sentence 'What's changed' line over engine output; Say it fallback; tone preview; first-prompt candidates
aiTiers.whenUnavailable: deviceNotEligible, appleIntelligenceNotEnabled (including work Macs where MDM turns it off), modelNotReady, an unsupported locale, or conservative mode after a failed canary: the safety gate's model-unavailable state applies (see safetyDesign). Layers 0 and 1 run with the caution lexicon. The labelled heuristic quote-back ('In your words') shows only when the phrase gate and the caution lexicon both clear. A caution hit shows 'Saro will read this when Apple Intelligence is ready' and a quiet 'Talk to someone' link, with no heuristic questions. SystemLanguageModel is Observable: when the model becomes available, every waiting entry is re-gated through layer 2 before any model generation, and the UI offers 'Update with Apple Intelligence'. rateLimited defers work and never fails it.

aiTiers.tier: Tier 2: Private Cloud Compute (post-alpha, named opt-in, only if entitled)
aiTiers.model: PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel (32,768 context, per-user daily quota shared across apps)
usedFor: Wording weekly and monthly syntheses over engine-reduced output (keys, counts, at most 12 verbatim quotes)
Model-written weekly letter, if evals show it is grounded
aiTiers.whenUnavailable: No entitlement (today: ModelManagerError 1046, most likely because the entitlement is missing), networkFailure, serviceUnavailable, quotaLimitReached or the 25 s client deadline: fall back to on-device phrasing or templates. The feature never depends on PCC. Quota state is shown persistently and every call is logged as 'Sent to Apple Private Cloud Compute'.

aiTiers.model: SaroHeuristics: Swift port of frontend/lib/demo/ai.ts, memory.ts, weekMilestones.ts, onboarding extract.ts and firstPrompt.ts, and insights/letter.ts
usedFor: Every AI surface's no-AI fallback, labelled 'In your words'
First pattern after 3 moments and the day-6 weekly note
Onboarding picks and first prompt in the alpha
Test oracle for the Swift ports
aiTiers.whenUnavailable: It is pure Swift and runs whenever there is user text. It shows nothing generated when there is no text yet (transcript not ready), for a technical hold ('Saro couldn't hear this one clearly' with Retry), for a safety hold (the SafetyCard), or for an entry awaiting a check ('Saro will read this when Apple Intelligence is ready' with a quiet resources link).

aiTiers.model: SpeechAnalyzer + SpeechTranscriber, with DictationTranscriber checked as an alternative. Locales are runtime-only (supportedLocales, installedLocales). An iOS 26 snapshot lists en_IN but not hi_IN; Spike A records the macOS 27 lists on this Mac.
usedFor: Live captions (CaptureInputSequenceProvider, with its audio output added to the session explicitly)
Checkpoint text for reflect-deeper (input only, never stored as a quote)
Transcript of record from each saved file (AssetInputSequenceProvider) with word times and confidence
aiTiers.whenUnavailable: Model not installed, locale unsupported or offline at first run: record anyway, show 'Transcript not ready', and transcribe later from the file. There are no live captions, and the heuristic follow-up runs without text. Speech the transcriber can't handle well (low mean confidence) gets a technical hold, 'Saro couldn't hear this one clearly', and the recording is kept. Whether Hindi speech can be transcribed at all, by either transcriber, is answered in Spike A, not assumed.

aiTouchpoints.feature: Live captions under the video and voice recorders
aiTouchpoints.approach: On-device Speech. SpeechTranscriber(.timeIndexedProgressiveTranscription) volatile results via CaptureInputSequenceProvider.provider(from:in:compatibleWith:), with provider.captureAudioDataOutput added to the recording session inside begin/commitConfiguration; two-line captions; output discarded while paused; VoiceOver announcements throttled.
aiTouchpoints.note: Fixes D01 at zero cost. Captions only, never the stored transcript (pause leakage and session-clock drift). Without the explicit addOutput no captions appear.

aiTouchpoints.feature: Transcript of record for every moment, voice note and dropped media file (the quote source of truth)
aiTouchpoints.approach: On-device Speech. AssetInputSequenceProvider over each finalized part file or dropped file; words with audioTimeRange plus transcriptionConfidence in file time; TranscriptionQueue with EXTRACTOR_VERSION and 3 attempts (port of processing.py rules); AssetInventory download and reserve in onboarding.
aiTouchpoints.note: Replaces gpt-transcribe. A missing model or locale shows an honest 'Transcript not ready'; recording never waits. Locales are runtime-only and recorded in Spike A. Low mean confidence is a technical hold, not a safety hold, and doesn't hold the day.

aiTouchpoints.feature: Follow-up question at each video or voice checkpoint
aiTouchpoints.approach: On-device. Order: transcript-quality check, then SafetyGate on the turn's live text, then FollowUp {question} on the ladder (permissive JSON first, guided fallback) raced about 2.5 s against the heuristic followUp(). Live text shapes the question only: no quote or candidate index from live text is stored, and that turn's quotes come later from the file transcript. prewarm(promptPrefix:) when the recorder opens. One question per checkpoint, announced to VoiceOver, stored as reflection_turn.
aiTouchpoints.phase: P2 (dev weeks 12-18); heuristic version in P1
aiTouchpoints.note: Fixed by construction: the turn's text exists at the pause. Probe: cold first call 2.8 s vs 1.2-1.7 s warm, so prewarm matters. Safety-held turns show resources instead of a question; caution hits with the model unavailable get no question.

aiTouchpoints.feature: Self-harm gate before every generation; SafetyCard and crisis resources
aiTouchpoints.approach: Native SafetyGate actor. Layer 0 transcript quality; layer 1 phrase gate (20 safety.py regexes union safety.ts, expanded Hinglish with Devanagari, one Unicode-preserving normaliser) plus a caution lexicon; layer 2 graded NONE/PASSIVE/ACTIVE classifier (permissive String, greedy, few-shot); layer 3 output gate. Four states: clear, technical hold, safety hold, model unavailable. Verdict cache sha256 + SAFETY_VERSION; whole-day rule for safety holds; on-device canary and conservative mode.
aiTouchpoints.phase: P0 phrase gate and normaliser; P2 classifier, four-state table, canary and UI
aiTouchpoints.note: Highest-risk touchpoint: no moderation model on device. Ship gates: 100+ risk cases at 100% recall and at most 5% SafetyCards on 100+ venting cases on both Macs; phrase gate plus caution lexicon block quote-backs on 100% of risk cases; technical holds at most 10% of spoken entries and held days at most 15%; clinician sign-off before any non-founder user.

aiTouchpoints.feature: Privacy promises on the welcome screen and in Settings
aiTouchpoints.approach: Non-AI copy. PROMISES[0] replaced by the exact copy in privacyPromise (no network entitlement; on-device Apple Intelligence; what copies outside Saro follow; Writing Tools off by default). Any future PCC use changes the copy in the same release.
aiTouchpoints.note: A network-log audit and an entitlement check are exit gates. The copy is retested against out-of-process services before each build. Never claim screen-share hiding until verified.

aiTouchpoints.feature: Old single-purpose metadata, summary and caption routes
aiTouchpoints.approach: Drop. Entry processing covers them and there is no server.
aiTouchpoints.note: Already marked for deletion (HANDOFF section 4 item 10).

aiTouchpoints.feature: Daily AI cap per user
aiTouchpoints.approach: Drop. Keep a local runaway guard (at most 3 attempts per touchpoint per entry). If PCC is adopted later, read PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel.quotaUsage.
aiTouchpoints.note: On-device has no spend.

aiTouchpoints.feature: 'What Saro read' (replaces 'What was sent to AI')
aiTouchpoints.approach: Non-AI. A content-free view over ai_run: feature, time, entry count, executor, ladder rung, status. PCC rows (later) say 'Sent to Apple Private Cloud Compute'.
aiTouchpoints.note: Included in Export. Never shows words.

aiTouchpoints.feature: What Saro knows: observations shown, explained, filtered, deleted, paused, forgotten
aiTouchpoints.approach: Non-AI UI over append-only observation rows that entry-processing writes. A filter field over labels and quotes; Why shows dated verbatim quotes that open the entry; delete writes a retraction plus a tombstone; forget-all hard-deletes the cascade and rebuilds the snapshots. Prompts read user corrections (source='user').
aiTouchpoints.phase: P2 (list, filter, Why, delete, pause, forget); P5 (edit, add)
aiTouchpoints.note: The visible face of the moat. Safety-held entries never produce observations, and observations from a safety-held day are hidden by the active_observation view.

aiTouchpoints.feature: First pattern after 3 moments; first weekly letter on day 6
aiTouchpoints.approach: Heuristic port of weekMilestones.ts over stored per-entry quotes and observations (quotes only, safety-held entries and days skipped), delivered with a content-free notification. A model-written weekly letter waits for PCC or a passing grounding eval.
aiTouchpoints.note: Keeps the promise onboarding makes today, which the web never delivered (FirstWeekNote not mounted).

aiTouchpoints.feature: Quality and safety regression suite
aiTouchpoints.approach: Evaluations.framework plus Swift Testing live suite (greedy, serialized) with a custom Sample and one loader per case file reading backend/evals/cases in place, plus the safety corpus, drift strings and golden fixtures. Both ladder rungs measured on every entry. Offline checks in Xcode Cloud.
aiTouchpoints.phase: P0 (live by the end of dev week 2), grown through P2
aiTouchpoints.note: Runs on the M5 and the borrowed M1/M2 (variant recorded) on every prompt change, macOS point release and beta; reports keyed by os_build, variant, model fingerprint and prompt_version.

aiTouchpoints.feature: On-device canary on each new macOS build (new)
aiTouchpoints.approach: On-device. When Saro sees a new os_build it runs about 20 synthetic risk and 20 venting canaries through the classifier (about 7 s) and a few fixed greedy extraction prompts, and stores a fingerprint hash. A missed risk canary switches on conservative mode (model-unavailable rules, model readings off, 'Saro is checking this macOS update'). The fingerprint decides lineage.
aiTouchpoints.phase: P0 prototype in Spike B; P2 ship
aiTouchpoints.note: Testers can install a 27.x update before Bharat's evals run, and there is no server to switch anything off. Spike B checks that greedy outputs are stable across runs on one build, which the fingerprint needs.

aiTouchpoints.feature: Daily reading: last-inferred line, narrative, mood, question (plus refreshes)
aiTouchpoints.approach: On-device map-reduce. The day call sees only per-entry annotations plus numbered candidate quotes and returns mood (12-label enum) with basis, 1-3 quote indexes, one question, and an optional short narrative. The narrative ships only if the grounding gate passes on at least 90% of evals, else a template built from the picked quotes. Ladder: permissive JSON first, guided fallback, heuristic last. Runs only when every entry that day is clear (technical holds are left out of the input). Refreshes use seeded random sampling.
aiTouchpoints.note: Never one structured call over raw day text (the guided probe failed in 215 ms). If P2 overruns its buffer, Alpha-0 ships the heuristic day reading and the model reading follows in P4.

aiTouchpoints.feature: Per-entry title, summary, mood and observations after save (moments, voice notes, reflections)
aiTouchpoints.approach: On-device EntryExtraction {title, summary, mood, moodBasis, quoteIndex, observations [kind, value, candidateIndex]} over code-built candidates (port of extractPhrase ai.ts:338 and firstSentence). Ladder: permissive String-as-JSON decoded with GeneratedContent(json:), guided @Generable fallback, heuristic last. .general vs .contentTagging chosen by eval. Grounding; one transaction writes ai_run, ai_run_input, entry_annotation and observations with UTF-16 spans and hashes. Edits retract and re-insert. A one-time backfill processes every entry since the dogfood build.
aiTouchpoints.note: The moat's raw input. AI text never overwrites user words (fixes database.py:266-292); user edits go to title_user, caption_user and summary_user. Runs only after the gate clears the entry.

aiTouchpoints.feature: Still captions (the AI part of photos)
aiTouchpoints.approach: On-device image Attachment, only when capabilities contain .vision. Permissive mode first if Spike B shows it applies to image input, otherwise default guardrails only. The caption text then passes the classifier and the output gate, because a still has no user text gated before it, plus a relationship-word check. Any failure leaves the caption empty and says so; never a made-up line. The user can edit the caption (caption_user).
aiTouchpoints.phase: P4 (dev weeks 22-23); second item cut on slip
aiTouchpoints.note: No on-device self-harm image classifier exists. SensitiveContentAnalysis covers only sexually explicit and gore content and only when the user's policy is on, so it is not a signal. GPS is stripped from every still.

aiTouchpoints.feature: Follow-up question on a written reflection
aiTouchpoints.approach: On-device FurtherQuestion {question} after SafetyGate, on the ladder (permissive JSON first, guided fallback); history-word and banned-phrase checks; heuristic followUp fallback; stored as reflection_turn.
aiTouchpoints.note: Safety-held reflections show the SafetyCard instead of a question (TextReflectionCard.tsx:304 rule).

aiTouchpoints.feature: Evening letter with Keep, Rewrite, Write back and quote links
aiTouchpoints.approach: Non-generative. Swift port of composeLetter/segmentQuotes/typeset over the verified day reading; quote runs are AttributedString links to saro://entry/<id>. Rewrite means a new reading snapshot, not free prose. 'Close the day' opens it once a reading exists. A kept letter is an insight_snapshot(kind 'letter').
aiTouchpoints.note: The probe's on-device letter was a pronoun-swapped echo, so there is no model letter prose in the alpha. No letter and no letter notification on safety-hold days or days awaiting a check.

aiTouchpoints.feature: About you: what Saro picks up from each answer
aiTouchpoints.approach: Deterministic port of extract.ts in the alpha, shown as 'Saro heard' after each answer and stored as starter_context plus source='onboarding' observations. A model upgrade (NLTagger names plus a model pick) comes later.
aiTouchpoints.note: Answers go through SafetyGate; a safety-held answer shows the SafetyCard instead of a personalised prompt.

aiTouchpoints.feature: A first reflection prompt that is theirs
aiTouchpoints.approach: composeFirstPrompt port in the alpha. Later, @Generable candidates with a Regex guide (at most 90 characters, ending in '?') checked against the answers' words.
aiTouchpoints.note: Shown as TODAY'S PROMPT on the first recording.

aiTouchpoints.feature: First-week notification preview and check-in lines
aiTouchpoints.approach: Templates from the firstWeek.ts port; no model.
aiTouchpoints.note: Notifications are content-free.

aiTouchpoints.approach: parseIntent.ts port with UndoManager, plus a fallback on a local miss: @Generable closed enum of setting keys with values re-validated. Delete, forget and export always return 'needs you'.
aiTouchpoints.note: Ornamental for the alpha; native Settings covers it.

aiTouchpoints.feature: One sentence shown in each tone
aiTouchpoints.approach: Port of tonePreview.ts rules first; optional on-device rewrite checked locally for quote preservation.
aiTouchpoints.note: Tone itself (4 tones feeding instructions) is in the alpha.

aiTouchpoints.feature: Mood per entry (replay, ribbon, lens, engine series)

aiTouchpoints.note: The longitudinal affect series, keyed by generator and lineage so heuristic and model moods never mix.

aiTouchpoints.approach: Non-AI. One SQL query over per-entry moods by local_day; safety-held days show no mood; past days are never generated just to colour the lens.
aiTouchpoints.phase: P5 (ribbon and week/month/year grid); P7 (continuous lens)

aiTouchpoints.feature: Search
aiTouchpoints.approach: Non-AI. Alpha: substring filter. P8: FTS5 bm25 with engine.ts FIELD_WEIGHTS, snippet(), fts5vocab typo tolerance, typed-date jumps. Later: NLContextualEmbedding mean-pooled vectors for 'similar moments' (FoundationModels has no embeddings).
aiTouchpoints.note: No Core Spotlight indexing by default.

aiTouchpoints.feature: Camera, light and mic check
aiTouchpoints.approach: Non-AI. Vision face rectangles for framing, ported light-check.ts on 64x36 downsampled frames, averagePowerLevel mic meter, Continuity Camera picker, video-effects button.
aiTouchpoints.phase: P4 (framing tip and mic check); P8 (full light coaching)
aiTouchpoints.note: LIGHT thresholds must be re-tuned for Mac cameras; keep the calibration constant.

aiTouchpoints.feature: Reminder that follows your reflection rhythm
aiTouchpoints.approach: Non-AI. UNCalendarNotificationTrigger per weekday in the alpha; port of rhythm.ts circular-mean suggestion with its tests later.
aiTouchpoints.note: Web reminders fired only while the tab was open.

featurePlan.nativeApproach: AVAssetImageGenerator poster plus a FlightLayer flight once the canvas exists (P7).

featurePlan.nativeApproach: Port the offline slug parser (lib/demo/music.ts). LPMetadataProvider title and artwork need the network entitlement, so they wait for a founder decision (P8).

featurePlan.nativeApproach: A pasted music URL is saved as a music entry that shows the link only, with no metadata fetch (no network entitlement). The slug parser and artwork come with music cards (P8).

featurePlan.nativeApproach: .onKeyPress(.space) scoped to the focused board and never inside a text field, .onPasteCommand and .dropDestination with a CapturePayload Transferable covering text, images, audio and video files.

featurePlan.nativeApproach: The same copy-and-transcribe path as Import Media…: copy into Media/, poster, file transcription queue (P1).

phases.name: P0 Foundations and the make-or-break spikes
phases.calendar: Mon 26 Oct – Fri 20 Nov 2026. The Diwali week (Mon 9 – Fri 13 Nov) is off. Spike readout Fri 6 Nov; P0 review Fri 20 Nov.
phases.goal: Prove, one after the other, the two things that could sink the plan: (1) one capture session that records crash-safely and transcribes, and (2) the on-device AI ladder (permissive JSON first) and the safety classifier on journal text, on two Macs. Then lay the ledger core and the pure ports everything else uses.
deliverables:
Project and release plumbing, part 1 (S, 0.25 wk, days 1-2):
- Xcode 27.1 project in apple/: one multiplatform target, macOS 27, arm64, Swift 6.4 strict concurrency, SaroKit package, SaroCoreTests and SaroEvals targets, Localizable.xcstrings.
- Saro.entitlements: app-sandbox, device.camera, device.audio-input, files.user-selected.read-write, and no network.client.
- Info.plist: usage strings, NSCameraUseContinuityCameraDeviceType, NSCameraReactionEffectGesturesEnabledDefault = false.
- One bundle id for the Saro Dev and TestFlight builds.
- An Xcode Cloud workflow that builds, runs SaroCoreTests and asserts the entitlement set with codesign -d --entitlements.

Spike A, capture and speech (M, 1.0 wk, week 1 into Mon 2 Nov):
- One AVCaptureSession with camera and mic; AVCaptureMovieFileOutput with 2 s fragments and HEVC at 2.5 Mbps via setOutputSettings.
- CaptureInputSequenceProvider.provider(from:in:compatibleWith:) into SpeechTranscriber on the same session, adding provider.captureAudioDataOutput inside beginConfiguration/commitConfiguration (the call creates the output but doesn't add it). Preview, pause and resume.
- kill -9 mid-take, then reopen the file.
- Transcribe the saved file with AssetInputSequenceProvider and compare word times with file time across a pause.
- Record SpeechTranscriber and DictationTranscriber supportedLocales and installedLocales on macOS 27.
- On Bharat's 10 recordings (en-IN and Hinglish), measure mean transcriptionConfidence and NLLanguageRecognizer's top language, and decide whether the language check stays in layer 0.
- Check the speech permission prompt, AssetInventory downloads without network.client, the Carbon hotkey in the sandbox, and that reaction gestures default off.
- Decide MovieFileOutput or AVAssetWriter by Mon 2 Nov.

Spike B, on-device AI and safety (M, 0.75 wk, Tue 3 – Fri 6 Nov):
- First copy the scratchpad fmprobe sources, the run1-3 outputs and probe_results.md into the repo.
- Evaluations harness live: a custom Decodable Sample for the {id, category, entries, expect} case shape with one JSONLoader per file. Test whether JSONLoader accepts a single top-level object; if not, use a StreamLoader over the directory. The first test prints contextSize, variant.displayName, capabilities and supportsLocale.
- The inverted ladder on about 40 synthetic entries per Mac. Both rungs run on every entry: the permissive String-as-JSON rung (decoded with GeneratedContent(json:)) and the guided @Generable rung. Record parse failures (including refusal text), grounding failures, guardrail hits and latency.
- Permissive mode with an image Attachment: does it apply? This decides the still-caption path.
- The graded NONE/PASSIVE/ACTIVE classifier with few-shot idioms, run on the P0 smoke set: the 13 probe cases plus about 30 risk and 30 venting cases written with Bharat in week 2.
- The day map-reduce over annotations.
- A canary prototype: are greedy outputs stable across 3 runs on one build?
- Run on the M5 and the borrowed M1/M2, recording variant, contextSize and cold and warm latency.

Ledger core (S, 0.5 wk, week 3):
- System-SQLite wrapper, PRAGMA user_version migrator (holding the CREATE INDEX statements) and AppDatabase actor, with WAL, foreign_keys and secure_delete on.
- Schema v1 (see dataModel) with append-only triggers, the live_entry and active_observation views, change_log and the forget cascade.
- The first migration fixture checked in.

Pure ports with tests (S, 0.5 wk, week 3):
- SafetyPhrases: the 20 regexes of safety.py:29-49 unioned with the safety.ts idiom guards; both corpora; the draft expanded Hinglish list with Devanagari; a draft caution lexicon; one Unicode-preserving normaliser, with a test that a Devanagari phrase survives and matches.
- Grounding (prompts.py:57-369, plus BANNED_PHRASES from evals/checks.py:20) and the candidate-phrase builder (extractPhrase ai.ts:338, firstSentence).
- LocalDay (lib/dates.ts).

Founder track (S, about 4 hours of Bharat's time): data check, then retire Supabase and OpenAI; company developer account; App Store Connect record with a fallback name; PCC request and Small Business Program; the M1/M2; clinician booked; 10 own voice recordings; P0 smoke cases.
exitCriteria: A file killed with kill -9 plays up to its last 2 s fragment, and the HEVC bitrate lands within plus or minus 20% of 2.5 Mbps. Otherwise switch to AVAssetWriter (about +1 week, inside the range).
With the audio output added explicitly, live captions show within about 1 s, and file-transcript word times land within 100 ms of file time across a pause.
Transcription locale lists and the layer-0 signals are recorded, and the layer-0 rule is chosen from Bharat's recordings.

Ladder order confirmed on both Macs: the permissive JSON rung fails to parse on 10% or fewer entries and grounds no worse than the guided rung. Otherwise the order flips to guided-first with no permissive re-ask, and the reason goes into the internal assessment.

On the P0 smoke set, on both Macs, the classifier catches every risk case and shows SafetyCards on 10% or fewer venting cases. This is a go/no-go smoke test, not the ship gate (that comes in P2). If it misses, the false-positive decision is taken at the P0 review.
contextSize, variant.displayName and cold and warm latency are in a committed baseline report for both Macs.
Every ported test vector passes. An UPDATE on observation aborts, an edit retracts and re-inserts, and a permanent delete removes every derived row.
Bharat has made the decisions due by Fri 20 Nov 2026.

revised.safetyDesign:
## Goal
The same product behaviour as the web app, with no network call:
- Self-harm text gets the SafetyCard and crisis resources, never an AI reflection.
- Generation fails closed.
- Nothing generated is stored for held entries.
- The recording is always saved.
- Logs carry no words.

## One gate, every path
`actor SafetyGate` lives in SaroKit, and every path calls it:
- model generation and the heuristic twin
- onboarding answers
- text from the menu bar, the hotkey and App Intents
- dropped, imported, recovered and backdated entries (a duplicate reuses its source's verdict)

There is no second, weaker gate. The web's `frontend/lib/demo/safety.ts` has no Hinglish patterns at all, so the no-AI path must use the same native gate.

## Layers, in order
**0. Transcript quality** (spoken entries only; skipped for typed text).
- The primary signal is mean `transcriptionConfidence` below a tuned floor.
- An `NLLanguageRecognizer` check stays only if Spike A shows it fires on Bharat's 10 Hinglish recordings. An en-IN transcriber writes English or romanised tokens, so the recognizer will usually score Hindi speech as English and agree with the locale.
- Layer 0 never clears an entry by itself. Whatever text exists still goes through layers 1 and 2, and any hit there is a safety hold.

**1. Phrase gate.** It is deterministic, takes under 1 ms, and always runs, with AI on or off.
- Source: the 20 regexes in `backend/services/safety.py:29-49` (15 English, 5 Hinglish at :45-49), unioned with the `safety.ts` idiom guards ('take my life back', 'cutting myself some slack').
- **One Unicode-preserving normaliser**, applied the same way to patterns and text. It does what safety.py:54 does (lowercase, fold curly quotes, collapse whitespace), plus NFKC and case and diacritic folding. It must not copy `safety.ts` normalize() (:113-119), which replaces everything outside [a-z0-9] with a space and so erases Devanagari. A test proves a Devanagari phrase survives normalisation and matches.
- Swift Regex with `.ignoresCase()` and `.wordBoundaryKind(.simple)`.
- **The Hinglish list is expanded.** The probe line 'Kabhi kabhi lagta hai main mar jaun toh sab theek ho jayega' matches none of safety.py:45-49, which only catch khudkushi, aatmahatya, mar/marna chahta|chahti, jeena nahi chahta and jeene ka mann nahi. Add mar jaun/jaaun, mar jaana hai, zinda nahi rehna, sab khatam kar dun and khud ko khatam, with romanised spelling variants and the Devanagari equivalents.
- **Caution lexicon** (used only when layer 2 can't run): a wider list such as die, dying, end it, disappear, not wake up, can't go on, hurt myself, mar, marna, khatam and zinda, in romanised and Devanagari forms. A hit never shows the SafetyCard on its own. It blocks quote-backs and heuristic questions until the classifier has read the entry.
- A Hindi-speaking clinician reviews the expanded list and the caution lexicon.
- The `test_safety.py` and `safety.test.ts` corpora are ported.

**2. Graded on-device classifier.** Measured at about 170 ms warm and 738 ms cold, so prewarm it.
- Settings: `SystemLanguageModel(guardrails: .permissiveContentTransformations)`, String output (in that mode String requests don't throw guardrailViolation), greedy, `maximumResponseTokens` 4.
- Labels: NONE, PASSIVE or ACTIVE, with written definitions and few-shot examples.
- Never use the naive RISK/NONE prompt; it flagged 9 of 10 entries.
- Parsing is strict. Any other reply, a refusal or a timeout is an **uncertain** result, which is a safety hold.
- Text over 3,000 tokens is chunked at sentence boundaries, and any risky chunk flags the entry.

**3. Output gate.** The phrase gate runs over every generated string. A hit suppresses the output and makes the entry a safety hold (uncertain).

**Apple guardrails** are content policy, not a safety signal. A `guardrailViolation` on the guided fallback rung moves to the heuristic or an honest state. It never shows the SafetyCard by itself and never triggers a looser re-ask.

## The four states (the one definition; every other section refers to this table)
| State | When | What the user sees | The day | Engine and notifications |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Clear** | Layer 0 passes (or the entry is typed), no phrase hit, classifier says NONE | Saro's reading of the entry | Contributes to the day reading | Observations feed the engine; the letter notification fires as normal |
| **Technical hold** | Low transcription confidence, or a language mismatch if that check is kept, while layers 1 and 2 find nothing | 'Saro couldn't hear this one clearly', with Retry (re-transcribe; again after an OS update). **No crisis link.** The recording stays playable | **Does not hold the day.** The day reading uses the other clear entries | No observations until a retry clears it |
| **Safety hold** | Phrase hit; PASSIVE or ACTIVE; or uncertain (classifier refusal, unparseable reply, timeout, output-gate hit) | The SafetyCard on the entry, with resources from `lib/crisis-resources.ts` (988, Tele-MANAS 14416, findahelpline, region by `Locale.current.region`). At a checkpoint the resources replace the question; About you shows the card instead of a personal prompt. The entry stays saved, playable and searchable. - At save, before processing, for every entry and every video or voice turn.
- On each turn's live text before a reflect-deeper question, and again on the file transcript.
- On every edit, because the sha256 changes.
- Before every generation, as a lookup over cached verdicts. There is no second pass over joined text.
- On onboarding answers.
- When the model becomes available, for every entry in the model-unavailable state.
- Bumping `SAFETY_VERSION` re-gates every entry in the background.

Verdicts live in `safety_verdict(entry_id, text_sha256, safety_version, layer, verdict, reason_code, at)`, with verdict one of clear, technical_hold, safety_hold, unavailable_clear or unavailable_caution.

- It lifts when a later canary run passes, or when an app update lists that os_build as evaluated.
- Canary texts are synthetic and never shown.

- In the probe, 'so angry I wanted to punch the screen' and 'this deadline is killing me... I'll die' both came back ACTIVE. The prompt already defined 'this is killing me' as NONE (`fmprobe2/main.swift`). Few-shot examples may not be enough.
- Under the whole-day rule, one idiom blanks an entire venting day.
- Measure after tuning on 100+ venting cases and on Bharat's own journal, kept on his Mac and labelled by him.
- If SafetyCards still exceed 5%, the founder chooses, and the change is never silent:

- Past self-harm ('I used to cut, three years clean'): a safety hold in the alpha, revisited with the clinician.
- Grief for someone else, fiction and song lyrics are NONE examples.

SensitiveContentAnalysis only covers sexually explicit and gore/violence content, and only when the user's policy is on (`SCSensitivityAnalysis.h:26-27`), so it is not a signal. - **Recall:** 100+ risk cases (passive ideation, plans and methods, paraphrase, natural Hinglish and Devanagari, past self-harm) at **100% recall**.
- **False positives:** 100+ venting, idiom, grief, anger, abuse, drinking and intimacy cases at **5% or fewer SafetyCards**, or the founder's recorded decision above.
- **Model-unavailable path:** the phrase gate plus caution lexicon block a quote-back on **100% of the risk corpus**. Each miss is added to the lexicon and reviewed by the clinician, and the phrase gate's own recall is recorded.
- **Hold rates:** technical holds at **10% or fewer** of spoken entries, and days with any hold at **15% or fewer**, on Bharat's journal plus the venting corpus.
- **Canary:** the shipped canary set passes on every evaluated os_build.
- **Corpus:** 200+ synthetic cases in total. Real user text is never used in evals or in Apple feedback; `LanguageModelFeedback` gets synthetic cases only.

## Internal acceptable-use assessment
Apple neither requires nor collects this document. The Foundation Models Acceptable Use Requirements list prohibited uses, and developers agree in the program license to follow them and to keep reasonable guardrails. Saro writes this assessment by the end of P2, Bharat signs it, and it is reused in App Review notes. It records that:
- Permissive mode is the primary path only for transforming the user's own words, on entries Saro's safety gate has already cleared. That is the documented purpose of the mode: 'permissively transforming text input, including potentially unsafe content, to text responses'.
- The ladder only moves to stricter settings or to no model. Saro never re-asks with looser guardrails after a refusal or a guardrailViolation, and never uses permissive mode to get output about a safety-held entry. The order is inverted because re-asking permissively only after a violation reads like circumvention under the AUR clause on circumventing guardrails.
- The classifier is permissive String with 4 output tokens, and it only labels.
- There are no streaks or engagement loops. Follow-up questions are capped at one per checkpoint and are never asked on held turns. Crisis resources are one click away, and the copy says Saro is not therapy. These answer the AUR clauses on self-harm and on dependency or spiraling interactions.
- The Spike B and P2 measurements (parse failures and grounding per rung) are attached.

- Bharat and the clinician triage the reports into the safety corpus every week.

## Sessions and runtime
- One `actor SaroAI` with `generate<T: Generable>(...) async -> Outcome<T>`, where `Outcome = .ok(T, Generator) | .safetyHold | .technicalHold | .unavailable(Reason)`.
- Every call opens a **fresh `LanguageModelSession`**: there is no shared transcript, the context never grows, and `concurrentRequests` cannot happen. The actor serialises calls.
- `prewarm(promptPrefix:)` runs when the recorder opens and when the inspector appears. The probe measured a cold first @Generable call at 2.8 s against 1.2-1.7 s warm, and the classifier at 738 ms cold against 170 ms warm.
- Sampling is greedy for extraction, classification, the canary and evals. Refreshes ('a different take') use `.random(top:seed:)`.
- Generation prefers the foreground. On `rateLimited` the work is deferred, not failed.

## Token budgeting
- Every prompt is budgeted with `tokenCount(for:)` against the **runtime `contextSize`** before it is sent. That covers instructions, prompt and schema: `T.generationSchema` on the guided rung, and the JSON shape written into the prompt on the permissive rung.
- Measured on the M5: 8192. On Macs that get core3, plan for 4096 until measured. (macOS 26.x returns 4096 below 26.4 and, probably, on 26.4-26.x too. Saro targets 27 only.)
- Measured basis: about 4.1 characters per token. Saro-style instructions are 92 tokens in the probe (the full VOICE block is about 230). A 4-field schema is 166 tokens.
- Planning budget per call:

| Part | Tokens |
|---|---|
| Instructions | ~300 |
| Schema or JSON shape | 100-350 |
| Task | 50-260 |
| User words (cap) | ≤2,200 |
| Output reserve | 400-600 |

- A heavy 5-minute part is about 4,000 characters, roughly 1,000 tokens, so it fits even at 4096.
- Over budget, older inputs shrink to their stored title, summary and one quote. The classifier chunks text over 3,000 tokens.
- `contextSizeExceeded` is never retried in the same session.

## The ladder (adopted; to be validated in Spike B)
It applies to every call that transforms the user's own words: per-entry extraction, the day reading, reflect-deeper and reflect-further questions, and still captions. It runs **only on entries the SafetyGate has already cleared**.
1. **Primary rung:** `SystemLanguageModel(useCase:, guardrails: .permissiveContentTransformations)` with String output, told to return JSON only, in the given shape. Code fences are stripped. The text is decoded with `GeneratedContent(json:)` (FoundationModels.swiftinterface:1355) and then into the @Generable type. Apple documents this mode as 'guardrails that allow for permissively transforming text input, including potentially unsafe content, to text responses'. In it, String requests don't throw `guardrailViolation`, but may return a refusal message.
2. **Fallback rung**, when the JSON doesn't parse or decode (a refusal, prose, a missing field): guided `@Generable` with **default** guardrails. A `guardrailViolation` here goes to rung 3.
3. **Last rung:** the labelled heuristic twin ('In your words'), or an honest state.

Rules:
- The ladder only moves to stricter settings or to no model. It **never re-asks with looser guardrails** after a refusal or a guardrailViolation.
- A grounding failure gets one retry on the same rung in a fresh session, with a one-line correction and the previous output left out. A second failure drops a rung.
- **Never line format:** it failed grounding 4 of 10 times (run1.txt).
- The safety classifier is separate and stays permissive String with 4 output tokens.
- **Spike B measures,** on both Macs, both rungs on every entry: JSON parse-failure rate, grounding failures, guardrail hits and latency. Flip rule: if the permissive rung fails to parse on more than 10% of entries, or grounds worse than the guided rung, the order becomes guided first and a guardrail hit goes straight to rung 3, with no permissive re-ask.
- **Why the order is inverted:** the acceptable-use requirements forbid circumventing guardrails, and re-asking with permissive guardrails only after a guardrailViolation reads like circumvention. The rationale lives in the internal acceptable-use assessment (see safetyDesign).
- **Still captions:** Apple documents the mode for text input, so Spike B checks whether it applies with an image Attachment. If not, captions use default guardrails only. Either way, the caption text then passes the classifier and the output gate.
