- **Quotes are verbatim by construction.** Code builds up to 24 numbered candidate phrases per entry (ports of `extractPhrase` ai.ts:338 and `firstSentence`). The model returns **indexes**, and code copies the text with field, UTF-16 span and `text_sha256`.
- Ported checks: `quote_in_source` (prompts.py:271), `_check_observations` (:316), `check` (:334), `HISTORY_WORDS` (:44; no 'again' or 'lately' without a history section) and `RELATIONSHIP_WORDS` (:49). `BANNED_PHRASES` comes from `backend/evals/checks.py:20` (`check_banned` :94); it was an eval check and becomes a runtime check here.
- **Noun-and-entity drift check** for any model prose (titles, summaries, the narrative, questions):
  - Every proper noun, number and person or relationship word must appear in the source.
  - Every content noun, lemmatised by `NLTagger` `.lexicalClass` and `.lemma`, must appear in the source or in a tunable allowlist of about 200 feeling and abstract nouns (day, evening, weight, feeling...).
  - Required test cases: it **must reject** 'the end of a long shift' ('shift') and the Hinglish title 'Thakawat aur asuvidha' ('asuvidha').
  - Known gap: invented relations between real nouns ('pushed through chai with Ravi') pass. That is why narratives stay at 1-2 short sentences, and a model narrative ships only if at least 90% of eval narratives pass the gate. Otherwise a template built from the picked quotes ships.
- The **phrase gate also runs over all generated text.**

## Principle
Keep the inputs perfect and treat everything derived as recomputable. The on-device model **extracts per entry** and, at most, **phrases** results. Code does the aggregating and diffing. That is why the alpha never blocks the diff/timeline engine: every input is stored with provenance and can be replayed into any future engine design.

## Atoms that never change meaning
- `entry` holds the user's own words (title_user, caption_user, summary_user, body) in columns no AI writes to. It also holds `captured_at` (UTC), `tz_id` (IANA) and `local_day`, which is frozen at capture, so series don't move when the user travels. A capture made while viewing a past day gets that day's `local_day`, `captured_at` = now and `backdated` = 1.
- `transcript_word` comes from the file pass. Each word has a file-time range and a confidence score, so any quote can open the exact second of the recording.
- `starter_context` holds the five About-you answers. They are also written as `source='onboarding'` observations, which form the **t0 baseline**.

## Extraction (per entry, at save, after the safety gate clears it)
- Code builds up to 24 numbered candidate phrases per entry. The model picks indexes and never types quotes.
- `observation` stores: `kind` (emotion|theme|person|intention), `key` (for example `person:maya`), `label`, `quote`, `field`, `span_start`/`span_end` (UTF-16), `text_sha256`, `local_day`, `ai_run_id`, and `source` (extractor|user|onboarding).
- A CHECK constraint requires a quote unless `source='user'`. BEFORE UPDATE triggers abort any update, so these rows are append-only. Hard delete happens only on Forget or Erase, because privacy wins.
- **Edits are retract-and-reinsert.** When the user edits an entry's text, or a re-transcription changes it, its observations get an `observation_retraction` row (reason `user_edited` or `source_edited`). Extraction then runs again and inserts new rows, and the retraction's `replaced_by` points to the new row. Nothing is ever updated in place, so the P0 test 'an UPDATE on observation aborts' and the edit flow agree.
- **Safety.** Safety-held entries produce **no** observations and leave only a content-free `safety_verdict` row. Observations from clear entries on a safety-held day stay stored, but the `active_observation` view hides them, so they never reach the engine, What's changed, the first-pattern note or the day-6 note. A re-gate that clears the day brings them back. Technical holds produce nothing until a retry clears them.
- **Duplicates** (`duplicated_from_id` set) never produce observations and are excluded from engine counts.
- **Backfill.** When model extraction ships in P2, every entry since the dogfood build is processed, so Bharat's December-to-March journal lives in a model series, not only a heuristic one.

## Gold labels, which outrank the model
- `source='user'` observations from memory edits and adds.
- User edits to title, caption and summary (`title_user`, `caption_user`, `summary_user`).
- `observation_retraction` with reason `user_deleted`, `user_edited` or `user_forgot_all`, plus `memory_tombstone` and `memory_pause`.
- In `day_state`: mood corrections (which lock the mood) and the answered question.
- `reflection_turn`: every question Saro asked and the user's answer. This is the highest-signal data in the ledger.
- `commitment` plus append-only `commitment_event` (created, carried, completed, let_go), carrying `carried_from_id`, so follow-through shows over weeks.

## Provenance and lineage
- Every artifact points to an `ai_run`, which records executor, variant, os_build, model_fingerprint, context_size, prompt_version, extractor_version and ladder_rung. `ai_run_input` records the exact windows the model read.
- **Series key = (observation key, lineage)**, where lineage is executor + variant + model_fingerprint + extractor_version + prompt_version. os_build is recorded on every run but doesn't split a series by itself. Heuristic output (`generator='heuristic'`) is its own series and is never diffed against a model series.
- **When the model changes**, the on-device canary computes a fingerprint for each new os_build:
  - Alpha: a changed fingerprint records a boundary and starts a new lineage, and the old rows stay. An unchanged fingerprint changes nothing.
  - From P5: re-extract history into the new lineage, eval-gated, so it only proceeds if the new extractor's report doesn't regress. It runs in the foreground or while plugged in and defers on `rateLimited`. Old rows are retracted with reason `reextracted`.
- `change_log(entity, id, op, at)` is written by the DB wrapper, so the engine knows what to recompute.

## Diff/timeline engine v0 (P5, dev weeks 24-26, by Fri 7 May 2027)
- Pure Swift plus SQL over `active_observation` and `commitment_event`, grouped by `local_day`. It makes no model calls.
- **Per-key series:** first seen, last seen, and counts per day and per week.
- **Window comparisons:** the last 7 days against the prior 21, and this month against last month.
- **States:** new, returning, rising, fading, gone quiet, steady. Thresholds are named constants that serve as calibration knobs.
- **Also computed:** person×emotion co-occurrence (with a minimum support), intention follow-through, and the mood series checked against user corrections.
- Every `Change` cites observation ids, which give dated verbatim quotes and source entry ids.
- Output is stored as `insight_snapshot(kind 'timeline'|'week'|'pattern', from_day, to_day, engine_version, input_hash)`. It is deterministic: the same ledger produces the same hash.
- **Wording:** templates by default. The on-device model may phrase 1-2 sentences over the computed delta, passing the same drift check. PCC, if granted, may only word engine-reduced output (keys, counts, at most 12 quotes), never raw history and never anything from a safety-held day.

## Testing the moat
- Two hand-written 8-week golden fixture journals with planted changes: a person who fades, a rising theme, an intention repeated then dropped, a mood shift, an os_build boundary with an unchanged fingerprint (no new lineage), and one with a changed fingerprint (new lineage). Each comes with its expected diffs.
- End-to-end mode runs real extraction over the fixtures and reports **planted-change recall** and **spurious-change rate** per variant and fingerprint.
- An edit test: editing an entry retracts and re-inserts its observations, and the engine output follows.
- A drift suite re-runs the corpus on each OS update and reports the rate of change the model alone causes.
- Bharat's own journal from Fri 18 Dec 2026 is the real-world check. The P5 exit requires at least 3 accurate 'what changed' lines and none invented.

## Surfaces
- **Alpha:** What Saro knows (with a filter and Why with quotes), the first pattern after 3 moments, and the day-6 weekly note.
- **P5:** 'What's changed', weekly and monthly, whose empty state says how many entries are still needed; and the week/month/year lens grid with mood wash.
- **P7:** emerging and fading themes overlaid on the lens, and the continuous pinch.
- **Later:** `NLContextualEmbedding` mean-pooled vectors (FoundationModels has no embeddings) for 'similar moments'.

- `self_claim_version` (append-only: statement, strength, status emerging|active|fading|contradicted|retired, `valid_from_day`, `valid_to_day`, `supersedes_id`, `ai_run_id`).

| `diagnostic_event` | kind (crash, hang), app_build, os_build, at | Content-free, from MetricKit MetricManager.diagnosticReports; feeds the Alpha report |
| `starter_context` | version, answers JSON, picks JSON (kind, text, value, utf16 start and end, question), first_prompt, ritual_time, at | The t0 baseline |
| `profile` | name, called, tone, focus_areas, memory_paused, onboarding_done_at | — |
| `change_log` | entity, id, op, at | Written by the wrapper |

## Views and indexes
- `live_entry`: hides trashed entries.
- `active_observation`: hides observations that are retracted, tombstoned, from trashed or duplicated entries, or from any local_day with a safety-held entry.
- Indexes are `CREATE INDEX` statements in the user_version migrator: `CREATE INDEX entry_local_day ON entry(local_day)`, `CREATE INDEX observation_key_day ON observation(key, local_day)` and `CREATE INDEX snapshot_kind_day ON insight_snapshot(kind, from_day)`.

## Later migrations
- **P5:** nothing new for backup-to-folder (the bookmark lives in UserDefaults).
- **P6:** CloudKit sync columns (`ck_system_fields`, `zone`).
- **P7:** `card_layout(entry_id, x, y, w, h, user_placed, z)`.
- **P8:** `entry_fts` FTS5 table (title, summary, body, transcript, tags; porter unicode61 remove_diacritics 2), plus an `fts5vocab` table for typo tolerance.
- **Engine design:** `text_embedding`, `self_claim`, `self_claim_version`, `claim_evidence`.

## Lifecycle rules
- **Trash** is a soft delete with one `trash_batch_id` per user action, undone by UndoManager. Items are purged after 30 days.
- **Forget and Erase** hard-delete across every derived row in one transaction, with one test per artifact type. Both also delete `Backups/` and take a fresh snapshot. Erase also covers Media, notifications, prefs and, later, the CloudKit zone. `secure_delete` overwrites freed pages.
- **Backups:** a daily `VACUUM INTO Backups/saro-YYYY-MM-DD.sqlite`, keeping 7. VACUUM INTO copies no free pages, and routine deletes age out within 7 days, which the privacy copy states. **Restore from snapshot** closes the database, keeps the current file as a pre-restore snapshot, and swaps in the chosen one.
- **Export** writes a `.saroexport` folder: JSON with an `export_version` field plus the media files. **Import** reads it back, idempotent by UUID. A round-trip test checks that rows and media sha256 match.
- **Alpha metrics** are computed, never stored as content. A session is a local day with at least one saved entry, counted by the local day of `captured_at` (so backdating doesn't create sessions), with duplicates excluded.

1. 'Saro has no account, no server and no way online. This version is built without permission to use the internet.'
2. 'Saro reads your words with Apple Intelligence, here on this Mac. Saro never sends what you record or write to us, to Apple or to anyone else.'
3. 'Your journal is yours. Export it, or erase it, whenever you like.'

- 'Where your journal lives. In Saro's folder on this Mac. Saro keeps 7 daily backups in the same folder so a mistake can be undone.'
- 'Deleting. When you empty the trash, forget something or erase everything, Saro deletes it and overwrites it in its database. Deleted items drop out of Saro's daily backups within 7 days. Forget all and Erase remove those backups straight away.'
- 'Copies outside Saro follow their own settings. If you use Time Machine, it backs up Saro's folder, and those copies follow your Time Machine settings (turn on backup encryption to protect them). An export you save to an iCloud Drive folder goes to iCloud. Text you copy follows your clipboard, which can reach your other devices through Universal Clipboard. On a work Mac, your employer's backup or management tools may be able to copy Saro's files.'
- 'Writing Tools is off in Saro's editors. If you turn it on, Apple's Writing Tools may use Private Cloud Compute, or ChatGPT if you've set that up, for the text you select.'
- 'The lock. Touch ID keeps people out of the app. It doesn't encrypt your journal. FileVault does.'
- 'Crash reports. If you share analytics with app developers in System Settings, Apple may send us crash and hang reports. They never contain journal text. Saro's Alpha report has no words in it, and it leaves your Mac only if you copy it into the survey.'
- 'What Saro read. A list of every time Saro's AI read an entry: when, which feature and how many entries. Never the words.'

## Later, only as a named opt-in (not in the alpha)
- A Settings toggle, off by default: 'Use Private Cloud Compute for weekly letters'.
- Its copy: 'When this is on, Saro sends a short summary of your week (themes, counts and up to 12 short quotes) to Apple's Private Cloud Compute to write your weekly letter. It never sends whole entries, and never anything from a day Saro held for safety. Each request is listed in What Saro read as Sent to Apple Private Cloud Compute.'
- Line 2 of the welcome copy changes in the same release.

## What makes it true
- **No network entitlement.** The alpha's sandbox has no `com.apple.security.network.client`. Xcode Cloud checks the signed app's entitlements with `codesign -d --entitlements` on every build. The P3 exit includes a network-log audit of Saro's process.
- **System downloads.** Apple Intelligence models and speech assets download through system services. Spike A confirms AssetInventory works without network.client. If it doesn't, the entitlement is added only for that, the network log is re-audited, and line 1 changes to what the log shows.
- **Writing Tools.** `.writingToolsBehavior(.disabled)` sits on every journal editor (SwiftUI, macOS 15+, present in the macOS 27 SDK), with the opt-in toggle above.
- **Deletion.** `PRAGMA secure_delete=ON`. Snapshots are `VACUUM INTO` copies, which carry no free pages, kept for 7 days. Forget all and Erase delete `Backups/` and take a fresh snapshot.
- **Exports.** The export panel warns when the chosen folder is in iCloud Drive, checked from the URL's ubiquitous-item resource values.
- **No third parties.** No third-party SDKs and no analytics. Spotlight indexing is off, GPS is stripped from stills, and logs and ai_run rows are content-free.
- **Crash data.** Crash and hang counts come from MetricKit's MetricManager on the Mac and are stored locally. Saro uploads nothing. TestFlight crash reports are sent by macOS under the user's own analytics setting.
- **Lock wording.** The Touch ID copy says lock, not encryption.
- **Screen sharing.** There is no screen-share hiding claim until it is tested on macOS 27 against Zoom, Meet and QuickTime.
- **PCC.** Only after Apple grants the entitlement, read from the provisioning profile. Whether PCC needs network.client is checked then, and the copy changes in the same release.
- **Retest.** Before each TestFlight build, the copy is checked against everything an out-of-process service can do (Writing Tools, Universal Clipboard, Time Machine, iCloud Drive, the Services menu), not only against the app's own connections.

## Testing
- **SaroCoreTests** (Swift Testing, offline, every push), covering:
  - grounding, the phrase and caution corpora, and the Unicode normaliser (a Devanagari phrase survives and matches);
  - heuristic twin vectors, and ladder JSON decoding (including refusal text and code fences);
  - append-only triggers, the edit path (retract and re-insert), the forget cascade, and secure_delete being on;
  - the export-erase-import round trip (rows and media sha256 match);
  - the state table, with one test per state, including 'no letter notification on a safety-hold day' and 'flagged-day observations excluded';
  - contrast ratios for every tint hour.
- **XCUITest suite** (scaffold in P1, grown through P3):
  - onboarding to first entry with AI on and AI off, using DEBUG toggles to force unavailable, force conservative mode and force each hold;
  - the recorder states, trash and undo, export and import, and Settings;
  - `performAccessibilityAudit()` on every screen (XCUIAutomation, macOS 14+).
- **Kill harness** (P1): a committed script starts a take, sends kill -9 at random points, relaunches, and checks the launch sweep: every file has a row, every row has a file, and the last 2 s fragment plays. It runs nightly on the M5 and before every build reaches Bharat.
- **Migration fixtures:** one checked-in saro.sqlite per PRAGMA user_version, migrated to head with invariant checks on every commit. Passing them is required before any build reaches Bharat.
- **AI-on/off matrix:** the XCUITest flows run in both modes, and the P3 and P4 exits are checked in both.
- **Eval suites on both Macs:**
  - SaroEvals (Evaluations.framework plus Swift Testing, greedy, serialized) runs on the M5 and the borrowed M1/M2 (variant recorded), plus an 8 GB M3/M4 if a tester has one.
  - It runs for every prompt change, macOS point release and beta, from a committed script that writes evals/reports/<date>_<os_build>_<variant>_<prompt_version>.json and diffs it against the last baseline.
  - Hosted CI has no Apple Intelligence, so these runs are local.
- **Differential check:** a local script runs the frozen TS heuristics over fixtures, and the Swift port's output is compared against it.

## CI
- **Xcode Cloud**, included with the Developer Program at 25 compute hours a month:
  - On every push to mac/*: build, run SaroCoreTests, and assert the expected entitlement set with `codesign -d --entitlements`.
  - On a tag: archive and upload to TestFlight.
- The repo's `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs only on the frozen web branch. Backend tests are deleted together with the runtime modules they import.

## On-device canary and conservative mode
- When Saro sees a new os_build, it runs about 20 synthetic risk and 20 venting canaries through the classifier (about 7 s at 170 ms each) plus a few fixed greedy extraction prompts, and stores a fingerprint hash of the outputs.
- If any risk canary is missed, Saro enters conservative mode:
  - classifier 'clear' verdicts aren't trusted, and the model-unavailable rules apply (phrase gate plus caution lexicon, quote-back only if both clear);
  - model readings are off, and a quiet banner says 'Saro is checking this macOS update';
  - the event goes into the Alpha report.
- It lifts when a later canary run passes, or when an app update lists that os_build as evaluated. Each build embeds the os_builds that Bharat's eval runs covered.
- A new lineage starts only when the fingerprint changes. Spike B checks that greedy outputs are stable across runs on one build, which the fingerprint needs.

## Alpha metrics (content-free and local)
- **Session** = a local day with at least one saved entry, counted by the day of captured_at, so backdating doesn't create sessions. Duplicates don't count. App opens are counted separately.
- **The Alpha report**, weekly in the app, shows:
  - days active, sessions in the first 7 days, and entries by kind;
  - ladder-rung counts, holds by state, and canary events;
  - crash and hang counts from MetricKit, stored locally as diagnostic_event rows. The source is MetricManager.diagnosticReports, the macOS 27 Swift API; MXMetricManager is deprecated in the 27 SDK.
- One click copies the report into the weekly survey. Sending it is part of each tester's 3-week commitment.
- TestFlight's per-tester sessions and crashes are an independent cross-check.
- By Alpha-0 (Fri 2 Apr 2027), Bharat writes down the thresholds, the definitions and the minimum number of active testers the iPhone-or-canvas rule needs.

## TestFlight logistics
- **Testers.** Internal testers must be App Store Connect users on the company team with a role (Admin, App Manager, Developer, Marketing or Legal), so only Bharat and the developer are internal. Alpha-0's 4 testers and the alpha's 15-30 are external testers.
- **Review.** The first external build goes to Beta App Review on Mon 15 Mar 2027, three weeks before Alpha-0. The review notes reuse the internal acceptable-use assessment, the not-therapy copy and the safety design. The P4 build with video may be reviewed again; allow a few days.
- **Expiry.** Builds expire after 90 days. A new build ships at least every 60 days until App Store 1.0. From 14 days before expiry the app shows the date and offers Export. Data survives expiry because the container stays.
- **Signing.** One bundle id for the Saro Dev and TestFlight builds, under the same team, so the journal carries across builds. A Developer ID build is only for Bharat's own Mac, if company enrollment lags. Signed under his individual account, it may not open the same container, so the journal moves by Export and Import.
- **Listing.** App Store Connect asks for privacy-policy and support URLs, so a static page (for example on the frozen demo's domain) is live before the first external build. The App Store Connect record is created in week 1 with a fallback name in case 'Saro' is taken. Age-rating and App Privacy answers are filled in during P3.

## Entitlements by phase (CI asserts the expected set)
- **P0:** com.apple.security.app-sandbox, device.camera, device.audio-input and files.user-selected.read-write (for export, import and the stills picker). Info.plist carries the camera, microphone and speech usage strings, NSCameraUseContinuityCameraDeviceType and NSCameraReactionEffectGesturesEnabledDefault = false. No network.client.
- **Developer ID fallback build:** the hardened runtime with com.apple.security.device.camera and device.audio-input.
- **P5:** files.bookmarks.app-scope, for 'Back up to a folder you choose'.
- **P6:** the iCloud (CloudKit) container and aps-environment for CKSyncEngine pushes, plus the iOS target's own set.
- **Later:**
  - the PCC managed entitlement from the provisioning profile, once granted;
  - network.client only if Bharat approves music metadata (P8), with the copy change;
  - In-App Purchase for StoreKit (P8).

## Accessibility (about 1 dev-week across P1-P3)
- Keep the web's in-app text size (0.9, 1, 1.125 and 1.25, plus 1.5), applied through the font-role helpers. macOS appears to have no system-wide Dynamic Type for third-party apps (to verify), so the system can't be relied on.
- Every colour token has Any, Dark and High Contrast variants. A unit test checks AA contrast for every tint hour.
- VoiceOver:
  - labels everywhere;

risks.risk: Safety recall without a moderation model. The graded classifier's 4 of 4 comes from 13 synthetic cases. Natural Hinglish ideation ('main mar jaun') was caught only by the classifier, and a mis-transcribed spoken crisis could slip past both layers. A false negative is real harm.
risks.mitigation:
- Low transcription confidence holds the entry, and layer 0 never clears text that layers 1 and 2 haven't read.
- An expanded, clinician-reviewed Hinglish list with Devanagari, under a normaliser that keeps Devanagari.
- One native gate on every path, failing closed: uncertain results are safety holds.
- 100+ risk cases at 100% recall on both Macs before any non-founder user, re-run on every prompt change and OS release.
- The canary catches a model update that breaks the classifier.
- Safety-held days never feed AI or the self-model.

risks.risk: Safety false positives. Idioms were labelled ACTIVE even though the prompt already defined them as NONE. Under the whole-day rule, one venting line blanks a day and shows crisis resources, which wears down trust.
risks.mitigation:
- Few-shot idiom examples, measured on 100+ venting cases and on Bharat's own journal.
- A pre-decided founder choice if SafetyCards exceed 5%: accept for Alpha-0, or per-entry scope.
- Technical holds (bad audio) no longer show a crisis link or hold the day.
- The rule is never changed silently.

risks.risk: The Mac is the wrong capture context. Video journaling is phone-native, desks are not where people unload, and testers may not reach 3 sessions in 7 days.
risks.mitigation:
- Voice is the default.
- Ctrl-Cmd-J, the menu bar and the floating pill give capture from anywhere.
- Content-free reminders at the user's quiet time.
- The habit metric (session = a local day with a saved entry) is measured from Fri 16 Apr 2027.
- A written rule on Fri 21 May 2027: if desk retention fails, the iPhone companion comes next.
- The codebase is multiplatform from day 1.

risks.risk: On-device readings feel thin, echo the user, or drift (probe: 'end of a long shift', 'pushed through chai with Ravi', a pronoun-swapped letter). Users then don't feel listened to, which is the core job.
risks.mitigation:
- Candidate-index quotes, map-reduce, and the noun-and-entity drift check tested on the probe strings.
- Model narrative only behind a 90% eval gate, otherwise a template.

risks.risk: A lost recording or wrong quote timing. MovieFileOutput plus the Speech audio output, the HEVC bitrate and the pause/file-time mapping are all unverified on macOS.

- Rows are written before the first frame, with a two-way sweep.

risks.risk: The schedule is still tight for one developer. Even at 23 dev-weeks, one person is a single point of failure, and the AI phase and capture are the likeliest overruns.
risks.mitigation:
- Spikes in sequence in a 3-week P0, and a week of buffer each in P1 and P2.

risks.risk: A macOS update changes the model on a tester's Mac before Bharat's evals run. The probe shows the classifier's judgement is fragile, and with no server there is no remote switch.

decisions.decision: Overall strategy for the Mac port
options: Ritual-first native alpha with the moat ledger underneath (this plan: Alpha-0 at dev week 21, alpha at dev week 23)
Faithful port to parity before any user (about 40 weeks to the alpha at the earlier sizing, more at this plan's sizing)
Moat-first: engine before capture (about 18-20 weeks at the earlier sizing)
Hybrid: React UI in a WebView, replaced surface by surface (alpha about 14-18 weeks at the earlier sizing, two runtimes until week 36)
decisions.why: It is still the fastest path to real people in daily use, and it tests whether people will journal on a Mac while writing every input the engine needs from the first entry. The honest re-sizing grows every option, not just this one. All three judges ranked it first.

decisions.decision: Default capture mode on the Mac
options: Voice first, video and writing one click away
Video first (as SARO-FJE-001 specified)
Text first
decisions.why: Talking to Saro is the product. Voice has no 'how do I look' friction at a desk, uses about 0.5 MB per minute against about 20 MB for video, and works from the hotkey over any app. The alpha measures the mix.

options: Ordered day board now; the week/month/year grid in P5; free-form canvas, continuous lens and lit ground in P7 once the habit is proven
Free-form canvas in the alpha (+6-7 weeks)
decisions.why: The canvas is the costliest port (9-11 weeks to parity) and isn't the moat. Card views are reused, so nothing is thrown away. The grid moves up to P5 so 'revisit over time' has a multi-day surface early.

options: System SQLite with a small in-house wrapper (no dependency)
GRDB 7 (new dependency, saves about 2 days)
SwiftData with a CloudKit-ready schema
decisions.why: SQLite 3.54.0 with FTS5 ships in the SDK. Triggers make append-only real, aggregates and search live in one file, and the schema can change freely while the engine is designed. SwiftData's CloudKit rules fight that. GRDB stays the fallback if the wrapper passes 3 days.

decisions.decision: Privacy promise, Writing Tools and Private Cloud Compute
options: On-device only for the alpha, no network entitlement, Writing Tools off in journal editors with a labelled opt-in; request PCC now and use it later only as a named per-feature opt-in
Allow PCC for letters at the alpha
Never use PCC
decisions.recommendation: On-device only, Writing Tools off by default, and request PCC this week.
decisions.why: 'Saro never sends your words anywhere' becomes provable through the sandbox, and the copy states honestly what out-of-process services do. PCC fails today anyway (error 1046, most likely the missing entitlement), and opt-in keeps the copy honest later.

decisions.decision: Fate of the web app and backend
options: Freeze the web app at ad4c7ed as the offline demo; delete Supabase, revoke the OpenAI key and purge Logfire after the data check; no importer
Same, plus your own web entries: dump them before deletion (about 2 hours), and build the importer in P5 (0.75 dev-week, moving later milestones by that)
Keep both running
decisions.recommendation: Freeze and retire. Dump your own entries now only if you might want them, and decide on the importer in P5.
decisions.why: It removes HANDOFF section 4's whole security backlog and the leaked anon key's reach (RLS was never applied), ends spend, and avoids two privacy stories. No self-model data exists in production. A dump costs 2 hours now and keeps the option open after deletion.

options: TestFlight under the company: you and the developer as internal testers, everyone else as external testers after Beta App Review; Developer ID only for your own Mac as a fallback; Mac App Store 1.0 at parity
Developer ID notarized download for testers
Give testers App Store Connect roles so they count as internal
decisions.recommendation: TestFlight under the company, with external testers and a Developer ID fallback for your Mac only.
decisions.why: Guideline 5.1.1(ix) prefers a legal entity for sensitive-data apps. TestFlight is a documented PCC channel, handles updates without Sparkle, gives crash data, and gives an early App Review signal. Internal testers need company roles, which outside friends shouldn't have.
decisions.decideBy: Fri 30 Oct 2026 (start enrollment now if needed)

options: English only (en-US, en-GB and en-IN as available at runtime); Hinglish covered by the expanded phrase list with Devanagari, the classifier and the caution lexicon
Promise Hinglish AI quality
decisions.why: Foundation Models has no hi_IN. Transcription locales are runtime-only, and Spike A records what macOS 27 actually offers, including DictationTranscriber, before anything is promised. Honest degradation beats wrong quotes.
decisions.decideBy: Fri 20 Nov 2026 (P0 review, after Spike A's locale lists)

options: Permissive JSON first on gate-cleared entries, guided @Generable fallback, heuristic last; never a looser re-ask (adopted, validated in Spike B)
Guided first, with any guardrail hit going straight to the heuristic and no permissive re-ask
Guided first, with a permissive re-ask after a guardrailViolation (the previous plan)
decisions.recommendation: Permissive JSON first; flip to the second option if Spike B shows worse parse rates or grounding.
decisions.why: Permissive mode is documented for transforming text input, including potentially unsafe content, which is a journal's normal content. Re-asking permissively only after a violation reads like circumventing guardrails, which the acceptable-use requirements forbid.
decisions.decideBy: Fri 20 Nov 2026 (P0 review, after Spike B numbers)

decisions.decision: Safety bar, day rule and overrides
options: Recall first, keep the web's whole-day rule for safety holds, no user override, clinician sign-off before any non-founder user
Recall first with an 'I'm okay, that was a figure of speech' override
Per-entry scope (only the flagged entry loses its reading)
decisions.recommendation: Recall first, keep the whole-day rule for safety holds, no override in the alpha. Technical holds never hold the day. If SafetyCards on venting text stay above 5% after tuning, accept up to 10% for Alpha-0 and revisit per-entry scope with real data.
decisions.why: A false positive costs a day's reading and shows resources. A false negative could put an AI reflection on a crisis entry. The probe's idiom false positives may not tune away, so the fallback is decided now, not silently later.
decisions.decideBy: Fri 20 Nov 2026 (P0 review, after Spike B numbers)

decisions.decision: What shows when Apple Intelligence is unavailable
options: A labelled 'In your words' quote-back, only when the phrase gate and the caution lexicon both clear; otherwise 'Saro will read this when Apple Intelligence is ready' with a quiet resources link; automatic re-gate later
Only an honest 'Saro didn't write about this one' with Retry
decisions.recommendation: The labelled quote-back under the caution rule.
decisions.why: It is grounded by construction and keeps the first 180 s useful while the model downloads, without letting a phrase-only gate guard quote-backs of risky text.

options: Full alpha scope (alpha at dev week 23, Fri 16 Apr 2027)
Move video, still captions and the Touch ID lock to v1 now (alpha about dev week 21-22)
decisions.recommendation: Keep full scope, and cut in the fixed order only if a slip happens.
decisions.why: Video is the second capture mode the habit metric needs to compare. The cut order is already agreed, so cutting early buys about 1.5 weeks at the cost of the answer.

decisions.decision: Model-written day narrative in the alpha
options: Ship it only if at least 90% of eval narratives pass the noun-and-entity grounding gate; otherwise a template built from picked quotes
Always template wording in the alpha (C's stance)
Always model prose
decisions.why: It keeps 'never invent content' while giving the model a chance to sound like it listened. The probe showed drift that quote checks alone miss.

options: 1080p HEVC at about 2.5 Mbps (about 19 MB per minute) with a 720p Space saver toggle
720p default
decisions.why: It looks good on Mac cameras and Continuity Camera, and a 5-minute daily habit stays near 35 GB a year. Voice-first keeps most entries tiny.

decisions.decision: What happens to history when Apple updates the model
options: The canary fingerprints the model on each new os_build; a changed fingerprint marks a boundary and starts a new lineage in the alpha; from P5, eval-gated re-extraction with old rows retracted
Always re-extract everything on any OS update
Freeze old observations forever
decisions.recommendation: Fingerprint boundaries in the alpha, eval-gated re-extraction from P5.
decisions.why: Boundaries cost nothing and never fake a change in the person, and the fingerprint stops point releases that don't touch the model from splitting every series. Re-extraction is free on-device but unmeasured in the background, so it waits until the engine needs consistent series.
decisions.decideBy: Fri 16 Apr 2027 (alpha launch, before P5 builds it)

decisions.decision: What comes after the alpha: iPhone companion or canvas
options: Written rule: if fewer than 50% of active testers (at least the minimum count set at Alpha-0) reach 3+ sessions (local days with a saved entry) in their first 7 days, or testers ask for on-the-go capture, the iPhone companion with sync comes next (default); otherwise the canvas comes next and the iPhone follows
Canvas next regardless
Mac only for v1
decisions.recommendation: Adopt the written rule, with the iPhone as the default next step.
decisions.why: Capture context is the biggest risk to the habit, and the paid tier as specced is 'privacy sync plus multi-device'. The rule turns the Mac premise into a falsifiable question with a pre-agreed response.
decisions.decideBy: Fri 21 May 2027 (end of dev week 28); thresholds and minimum tester count written down by Fri 2 Apr 2027

decisions.decision: Business model and App Store timing
options: Free alpha; App Store 1.0 at parity as a free core plus 'Saro+' (one-time or annual) covering the iPhone app, sync and PCC features
An earlier free Mac 1.0 after P5, adding Saro+ with the iPhone and sync
Paid upfront
decisions.recommendation: The first option as the default, confirmed at the gate with the alpha data.
decisions.why: Zero server cost makes a one-time price or a generous free tier possible. The paid features depend on the iPhone decision, the Guideline 5.1.3 answer and PCC, all known by May. StoreKit without network.client is checked in P3, and StoreKit work sits in P8.

options: One Swift developer throughout (alpha dev week 23, parity with the iPhone about dev week 56)
Add a contract developer at the iPhone-or-canvas call, taking the track the rule doesn't put first (parity with the iPhone about dev week 47)
decisions.recommendation: One developer to the alpha; decide the second developer at the iPhone-or-canvas call.
decisions.why: The alpha path is sequential and gains little from a second person. After the call, the canvas and the iPhone work run in parallel well, and starting the canvas before the habit is proven would contradict the rule.

issues.where: safetyDesign > The four states table; aiPipeline > Day reading ('an entry awaiting a check stops it'); architecture Notifications row; aiTouchpoints evening-letter, week-milestones, reflect-deeper; featurePlan 'Close the day' and 'Evening letter notification'; aiTiers Speech.whenUnavailable
issues.problem: The one state table leaves gaps the other sections lean on. (a) It sets no precedence. A low-confidence spoken entry on a Mac where the model is unavailable could be read as a technical hold (no crisis link, day not held) or as model unavailable (caution rules). The technical-hold row needs 'layers 1 and 2 find nothing', but layer 2 can't run there. (b) 'Days awaiting a check' or 'still waiting for a safety check' is used in at least 6 places but never defined in the table. The table only says 'a day with a caution hit waits'. (c) Entries with no verdict yet (transcript not ready) are in no state. So a day reading, letter and letter notification can go out while a crisis voice note is still untranscribed. The first-pattern and day-6 notes skip only safety-held entries, so a caution-hit quote can surface there. And Speech.whenUnavailable has 'the heuristic follow-up runs without text', which asks a question on a turn that was never gated.
issues.fix: Add under the table: 'Precedence: safety hold > model unavailable > technical hold > clear. A technical hold requires layer 2 to have run. Awaiting a check = a model-unavailable entry with a caution hit, or any entry with no verdict yet (transcript not ready). A day with such an entry gets no day reading, letter or letter notification until it is gated. Such entries are excluded from the first-pattern and day-6 notes. A checkpoint turn with no live text shows Keep going and no follow-up question.' In aiTiers Speech.whenUnavailable, change 'the heuristic follow-up runs without text' to 'no follow-up question; the checkpoint shows Keep going'. In aiTouchpoints.week-milestones and the featurePlan 'First pattern' row, change 'safety-held entries and days skipped' to 'safety-held and awaiting-a-check entries, and safety-held days, skipped'.
